cbor.description: Signable canonical CBOR (RFC 8949), pure loft — canonical map-key ordering, full decode, byte-identical encode->decode->encode, native == wasm.

api.sig: pub enum CborValue
api.doc:
A dynamic CBOR value.  Mirrors the stdlib `JsonValue`, with CBOR's extra
`CBytes` (native byte string) and the integer split that CBOR makes at the
wire level folded into one signed `CInt`.

api.sig: pub struct CborEntry
api.doc: One key/value pair of a `CMap`.

api.sig: pub fn encode(v: CborValue) -> vector<u8>
api.doc: Encode a `CborValue` to canonical CBOR bytes.

api.sig: pub struct Decoded
api.doc:
The result of decoding one CBOR value: the `value`, the byte position just
past it (`next`), and `ok` — false on any malformed / non-canonical /
truncated input.  Decoding never crashes (loft-safe): a bad byte stream
yields ok=false rather than a trap.

api.sig: pub fn decode(bytes: vector<u8>) -> Decoded
api.doc:
Decode canonical CBOR bytes into a `CborValue`.  Returns `ok=false` on any
malformed, non-canonical, or truncated input — and rejects trailing bytes
after the top-level value.  Never crashes.

api.doc:

api.sig: pub fn decode(bytes: vector<u8>) -> Decoded
api.doc:
Decode canonical CBOR bytes into a `CborValue`.  Returns `ok=false` on any

api.sig: pub enum CborValue
api.doc:
A dynamic CBOR value.  Mirrors the stdlib `JsonValue`, with CBOR's extra
`CBytes` (native byte string) and the integer split that CBOR makes at the
wire level folded into one signed `CInt`.
Example: @CBR-002 — which variant you pick is part of the wire form: the same
two payload bytes are a different record as `CBytes` than as `CText`.

api.sig: pub struct CborEntry
api.doc: One key/value pair of a `CMap`.

api.sig: pub fn encode(v: CborValue) -> vector<u8>
api.doc:
Encode a `CborValue` to canonical CBOR bytes.
A map's entries are SORTED here by their encoded key bytes, so the order you
built the map in never reaches the wire.
Example: @CBR-001 — two maps built in opposite orders encode identically, which
is what keeps a signature over the bytes valid.
Example: @CBR-002 — `CBytes` and `CText` are different wire types, so the
loft-side choice is part of what gets signed.
Example: @CBR-004 — canonical is about ORDER, not uniqueness: duplicate keys
encode without complaint.

api.sig: pub struct Decoded
api.doc:
The result of decoding one CBOR value: the `value`, the byte position just
past it (`next`), and `ok` — false on any malformed / non-canonical /
truncated input.  Decoding never crashes (loft-safe): a bad byte stream
yields ok=false rather than a trap.

api.sig: pub fn decode(bytes: vector<u8>) -> Decoded
api.doc:
Decode canonical CBOR bytes into a `CborValue`.  Returns `ok=false` on any
malformed, non-canonical, or truncated input — and rejects trailing bytes
after the top-level value.  Never crashes.
Example: @CBR-003 — `ok=false` is one answer for four different problems, and
the surprising one is that well-formed but NON-canonical CBOR is refused.
Example: @CBR-004 — a map carrying two entries under one key decodes ok=true.

crypto.description: Cryptographic primitives — SHA-256, HMAC, base64; Ed25519, X25519, HPKE (RFC 9180), ChaCha20-Poly1305 / XChaCha20-Poly1305 / AES-256-GCM, HKDF, OS CSPRNG.

api.sig: pub fn sha256(data: text) -> text
api.doc: SHA-256 hash of a string. Returns 64-char hex string.

api.sig: pub fn sha256_b64(data_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
SHA-256 of the RAW BYTES decoded from base64 `data_b64`. Returns base64 of the
32-byte digest. Use this to hash arbitrary byte strings (ciphertext, canonical
CBOR) that are not valid UTF-8 and so cannot be passed to `sha256` as text.

api.sig: pub fn hmac_sha256(key: text, data: text) -> text
api.doc: HMAC-SHA256 of data with key. Returns 64-char hex string.

api.sig: pub fn base64_encode(data: text) -> text
api.doc: Base64 encode a string.

api.sig: pub fn base64_decode(data: text) -> text
api.doc: Base64 decode a string.

api.sig: pub fn base64url_encode(data: text) -> text
api.doc: Base64url encode (JWT-safe, no padding).

api.sig: pub fn ed25519_public_key(secret_key_b64: text) -> text
api.doc: Derive the 32-byte public key (base64) from a 32-byte secret seed (base64).

api.sig: pub fn ed25519_sign(secret_key_b64: text, message_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
Sign the base64 `message` bytes with the 32-byte secret seed (base64).
Returns the 64-byte signature, base64.

api.sig: pub fn ed25519_verify(public_key_b64: text, message_b64: text, signature_b64: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Verify a signature over the base64 `message` bytes under a public key.
Returns true iff the signature is valid.

api.sig: pub fn x25519_dh(secret_key_b64: text, public_key_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
A secret key is a 32-byte X25519 scalar (base64); a public key is the
32-byte u-coordinate (base64).  Returns the raw 32-byte shared secret
(base64), or "" if either input is the wrong length.  Run the result
through `hkdf_sha256` before using it as a key (RFC 7748 §6.1).

api.sig: pub fn hkdf_sha256(salt_b64: text, ikm_b64: text, info_b64: text, length: integer) -> text
api.doc:
Derive `length` bytes of output keying material from `ikm`, `salt`, and
`info` (each base64).  An empty base64 `salt` selects the all-zero salt.
Returns the base64 OKM, or "" if `length` exceeds 255*32 or is <= 0.

api.sig: pub fn hkdf_extract(salt_b64: text, ikm_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
HKDF-Extract (RFC 5869 §2.2): the 32-byte PRK (base64) HMAC-SHA256(salt, ikm).
An empty base64 `salt` selects the all-zero salt.  Use the Extract/Expand
halves directly (rather than `hkdf_sha256`) when a PRK is reused for several
Expands or when an Extract output is itself the value you want (e.g. HPKE).

api.sig: pub fn hkdf_expand(prk_b64: text, info_b64: text, length: integer) -> text
api.doc:
HKDF-Expand (RFC 5869 §2.3) from an existing 32-byte PRK.  Returns `length`
bytes of OKM (base64), or "" on a short PRK, length > 255*32, or length <= 0.

api.sig: pub fn bytes_to_base64(bytes: vector<u8>) -> text
api.doc: Standard base64 of a raw byte vector.  Empty vector -> "".

api.sig: pub fn base64_to_bytes(b64: text) -> vector<u8>
api.doc:
Raw bytes from standard base64.  Malformed / empty input -> empty vector.
See the CAUTION above: read the result, never `+=` onto it.

api.sig: pub fn aes256gcm_seal(key_b64: text, nonce_b64: text, aad_b64: text, plaintext_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
Encrypt + authenticate `plaintext` under `key`/`nonce`, binding `aad`.
Returns base64 of ciphertext WITH the 16-byte tag appended, or "" on bad
key/nonce length.

api.sig: pub fn aes256gcm_open(key_b64: text, nonce_b64: text, aad_b64: text, ciphertext_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
Verify + decrypt `ciphertext` (ciphertext||tag, base64) under `key`/`nonce`,
binding `aad`.  Returns the base64 plaintext, or "" on ANY authentication
failure — an empty result means the ciphertext/tag/aad did not verify.

api.sig: pub fn random_bytes(length: integer) -> text
api.doc:
Return `length` cryptographically secure random bytes (base64) from the OS
RNG.  Returns "" for length <= 0.  Use for keys (32), nonces (12), salts.

api.sig: pub struct HpkeSealed
api.doc:
The result of `hpke_seal_base`: the KEM-encapsulated key `enc` and the AEAD
`ciphertext` (ciphertext||16-byte-tag), both base64.

api.sig: pub fn hpke_seal_base(pk_r_b64: text, info_b64: text, aad_b64: text, pt_b64: text) -> HpkeSealed
api.doc:
HPKE SealBase (RFC 9180 §6.1): encrypt `pt` to recipient public key `pk_r`,
binding `info` (key-schedule context) and `aad` (per-message AAD).  Generates
a fresh ephemeral key, so each call's output differs.  All args/fields base64.
Returns HpkeSealed { enc, ciphertext }; both "" on failure.

api.sig: pub fn hpke_seal_base_deterministic(pk_r_b64: text, sk_e_b64: text, info_b64: text, aad_b64: text, pt_b64: text) -> HpkeSealed
api.doc:
Deterministic SealBase — TEST ONLY.  Uses the caller-supplied ephemeral
secret `sk_e_b64` instead of a random one, so the output is reproducible
against an RFC 9180 known-answer vector.  Never use in production.

api.sig: pub fn hpke_open_base(sk_r_b64: text, enc_b64: text, info_b64: text, aad_b64: text, ct_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
HPKE OpenBase (RFC 9180 §6.1): decrypt `ct` for recipient secret key `sk_r`
using the sender's `enc`, binding `info` and `aad`.  All args base64.  Returns
the base64 plaintext, or "" on ANY failure (bad enc/key or AEAD auth failure).

api.sig: pub fn hpke_key_schedule_base_for_test(shared_secret_b64: text, info_b64: text) -> (text, text)
api.doc:
Expose the key-schedule outputs for KAT assertions — TEST ONLY.  Given a
shared secret and base64 `info`, returns (key_b64, base_nonce_b64).

api.sig: pub fn hpke_encap_deterministic_for_test(pk_r_b64: text, sk_e_b64: text) -> (text, text)
api.doc:
Expose deterministic Encap for KAT assertions — TEST ONLY.  Returns
(shared_secret_b64, enc_b64).

api.sig: pub fn sha256_b64(data_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
SHA-256 of the RAW BYTES decoded from base64 `data_b64`. Returns base64 of the
32-byte digest. Use this to hash arbitrary byte strings (ciphertext, canonical
CBOR) that are not valid UTF-8 and so cannot be passed to `sha256` as text.
Example: @CRY-001 — the two hashing doors: text in / hex out vs base64 both ways.

api.sig: pub fn hmac_sha256(key: text, data: text) -> text
api.doc: HMAC-SHA256 of data with key. Returns 64-char hex string.

api.sig: pub fn base64_encode(data: text) -> text
api.doc: Base64 encode a string.

api.sig: pub fn base64_decode(data: text) -> text
api.doc: Base64 decode a string.

api.sig: pub fn base64url_encode(data: text) -> text
api.doc: Base64url encode (JWT-safe, no padding).

api.sig: pub fn ed25519_public_key(secret_key_b64: text) -> text
api.doc: Derive the 32-byte public key (base64) from a 32-byte secret seed (base64).

api.sig: pub fn ed25519_sign(secret_key_b64: text, message_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
Sign the base64 `message` bytes with the 32-byte secret seed (base64).
Returns the 64-byte signature, base64.
Example: @CRY-002 — sign `base64_encode(msg)`; the bare text signs other bytes, silently.

api.sig: pub fn ed25519_verify(public_key_b64: text, message_b64: text, signature_b64: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Verify a signature over the base64 `message` bytes under a public key.
Returns true iff the signature is valid.
Example: @CRY-002 — why a wrongly-spelled message still verifies against itself.

api.sig: pub fn ecdsa_p256_keygen() -> text
api.doc: Generate a fresh 32-byte P-256 secret scalar (base64) from the OS CSPRNG.

api.sig: pub fn ecdsa_p256_public_key(secret_key_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
Derive the 64-byte public key `x || y` (base64) from a 32-byte secret scalar (base64).
Example: @CRY-003 — the three JOSE lengths (32 / 64 / 64) a caller should check.

api.sig: pub fn ecdsa_p256_sign(secret_key_b64: text, message_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
Sign the base64 `message` bytes with the 32-byte secret scalar (base64).
Returns the 64-byte `r || s` signature (base64), deterministic per RFC 6979.
Example: @CRY-003 — signing twice answers identical bytes, and `r || s` is not DER.

api.sig: pub fn ecdsa_p256_verify(public_key_b64: text, message_b64: text, signature_b64: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Verify an ES256 signature (64-byte `r || s`) over the base64 `message` bytes
under a 64-byte `x || y` public key.  Returns true iff the signature is valid.

api.sig: pub fn x25519_dh(secret_key_b64: text, public_key_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
A secret key is a 32-byte X25519 scalar (base64); a public key is the
32-byte u-coordinate (base64).  Returns the raw 32-byte shared secret
(base64), or "" if either input is the wrong length.  Run the result
through `hkdf_sha256` before using it as a key (RFC 7748 §6.1).
Example: @CRY-004 — the DH output is keying material, not a key; and how to get a
public key out of a secret scalar (X25519 has no separate keygen).

api.sig: pub fn hkdf_sha256(salt_b64: text, ikm_b64: text, info_b64: text, length: integer) -> text
api.doc:
Derive `length` bytes of output keying material from `ikm`, `salt`, and
`info` (each base64).  An empty base64 `salt` selects the all-zero salt.
Returns the base64 OKM, or "" if `length` exceeds 255*32 or is <= 0.
Example: @CRY-004 — `info` is what separates two keys from one shared secret.

api.sig: pub fn hkdf_extract(salt_b64: text, ikm_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
HKDF-Extract (RFC 5869 §2.2): the 32-byte PRK (base64) HMAC-SHA256(salt, ikm).
An empty base64 `salt` selects the all-zero salt.  Use the Extract/Expand
halves directly (rather than `hkdf_sha256`) when a PRK is reused for several
Expands or when an Extract output is itself the value you want (e.g. HPKE).
Example: @CRY-004 — the split halves compose to exactly `hkdf_sha256`.

api.sig: pub fn hkdf_expand(prk_b64: text, info_b64: text, length: integer) -> text
api.doc:
HKDF-Expand (RFC 5869 §2.3) from an existing 32-byte PRK.  Returns `length`
bytes of OKM (base64), or "" on a short PRK, length > 255*32, or length <= 0.

api.sig: pub fn bytes_to_base64(bytes: vector<u8>) -> text
api.doc: Standard base64 of a raw byte vector.  Empty vector -> "".

api.sig: pub fn base64_to_bytes(b64: text) -> vector<u8>
api.doc:
Raw bytes from standard base64.  Malformed / empty input -> empty vector.
See the CAUTION above: read the result, never `+=` onto it.
Example: @CRY-001 — reading a decoded byte vector, and hashing non-UTF-8 bytes.

api.sig: pub fn aes256gcm_seal(key_b64: text, nonce_b64: text, aad_b64: text, plaintext_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
Encrypt + authenticate `plaintext` under `key`/`nonce`, binding `aad`.
Returns base64 of ciphertext WITH the 16-byte tag appended, or "" on bad
key/nonce length.
Example: @CRY-005 — the tag rides in the blob, and a fresh nonce per message.

api.sig: pub fn aes256gcm_open(key_b64: text, nonce_b64: text, aad_b64: text, ciphertext_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
Verify + decrypt `ciphertext` (ciphertext||tag, base64) under `key`/`nonce`,
binding `aad`.  Returns the base64 plaintext, or "" on ANY authentication
failure — an empty result means the ciphertext/tag/aad did not verify.
Example: @CRY-005 — "" is a failure signal, and an authentic empty plaintext gives it too.

api.sig: pub fn random_bytes(length: integer) -> text
api.doc:
Return `length` cryptographically secure random bytes (base64) from the OS
RNG.  Returns "" for length <= 0.  Use for keys (32), nonces (12), salts.

api.sig: pub struct HpkeSealed
api.doc:
The result of `hpke_seal_base`: the KEM-encapsulated key `enc` and the AEAD
`ciphertext` (ciphertext||16-byte-tag), both base64.

api.sig: pub fn hpke_seal_base(pk_r_b64: text, info_b64: text, aad_b64: text, pt_b64: text) -> HpkeSealed
api.doc:
HPKE SealBase (RFC 9180 §6.1): encrypt `pt` to recipient public key `pk_r`,
binding `info` (key-schedule context) and `aad` (per-message AAD).  Generates
a fresh ephemeral key, so each call's output differs.  All args/fields base64.
Returns HpkeSealed { enc, ciphertext }; both "" on failure.
Example: @CRY-006 — `enc` is fresh per call and must travel with the ciphertext.

api.sig: pub fn hpke_seal_base_deterministic(pk_r_b64: text, sk_e_b64: text, info_b64: text, aad_b64: text, pt_b64: text) -> HpkeSealed
api.doc:
Deterministic SealBase — TEST ONLY.  Uses the caller-supplied ephemeral
secret `sk_e_b64` instead of a random one, so the output is reproducible
against an RFC 9180 known-answer vector.  Never use in production.

api.sig: pub fn hpke_open_base(sk_r_b64: text, enc_b64: text, info_b64: text, aad_b64: text, ct_b64: text) -> text
api.doc:
HPKE OpenBase (RFC 9180 §6.1): decrypt `ct` for recipient secret key `sk_r`
using the sender's `enc`, binding `info` and `aad`.  All args base64.  Returns
the base64 plaintext, or "" on ANY failure (bad enc/key or AEAD auth failure).
Example: @CRY-006 — `info` AND `aad` must both match the sender's, or open gives "".

api.sig: pub fn hpke_key_schedule_base_for_test(shared_secret_b64: text, info_b64: text) -> (text, text)
api.doc:
Expose the key-schedule outputs for KAT assertions — TEST ONLY.  Given a
shared secret and base64 `info`, returns (key_b64, base_nonce_b64).

api.sig: pub fn hpke_encap_deterministic_for_test(pk_r_b64: text, sk_e_b64: text) -> (text, text)
api.doc:
Expose deterministic Encap for KAT assertions — TEST ONLY.  Returns
(shared_secret_b64, enc_b64).

api.doc: Circle shape for 2D collision.

api.sig: pub fn rects_overlap(a: const Rect, b: const Rect) -> boolean
api.doc:
Test whether two axis-aligned rectangles overlap.
The comparison is STRICT, so rectangles sharing an edge do NOT overlap.
Example: @SHP-001 — touching is not overlapping, and what that buys: a row of
abutting tiles is quiet, and a mover pushed out by exactly its penetration
depth is done.

api.sig: pub fn circles_overlap(a: const Circle, b: const Circle) -> boolean
api.doc:
Test whether two circles overlap.
Strict, like `rects_overlap`: tangent circles do NOT overlap.
Example: @SHP-001 — the shared strict boundary across all three predicates.

api.sig: pub fn rect_circle_overlap(r: const Rect, c: const Circle) -> boolean
api.doc:
Test whether a rectangle and a circle overlap.
A true circle test — the circle's bounding box is NOT a substitute for it, and
a circle wholly inside the rectangle counts as overlapping.
Example: @SHP-003 — where the box approximation disagrees (every corner), and
why containment answers true.

api.sig: pub struct Overlap
api.doc: Overlap depth between two rectangles on each axis.

api.sig: pub fn rect_overlap_depth(a: const Rect, b: const Rect) -> Overlap
api.doc:
Compute the overlap depth between two rectangles on each axis.
Both depths are UNSIGNED distances — the caller derives the direction from the
relative positions.  Returns (0.0, 0.0) when they don't overlap.
Useful for bounce direction: if ox < oy → horizontal bounce.
Example: @SHP-002 — the sign is the caller's to work out (applying it the wrong
way pushes deeper), and the smaller axis is the minimal correction.

api.sig: pub fn aabb_overlap(ax: float, ay: float, aw: float, ah: float,
api.doc:

Same strict boundary as `rects_overlap`.

api.sig: pub fn aabb_depth_x(ax: float, ay: float, aw: float, ah: float,
api.doc:

`aabb_depth_y` is the other half of the pair, and each call re-runs the overlap
test on its own.  Unsigned, like `rect_overlap_depth`.  `0.0` means the two do
not overlap AT ALL (a real overlap always penetrates by strictly more than
zero), not "they meet with no penetration on this axis".

into a correction.

into a correction.

api.sig: pub struct Proxy
api.doc:
A shape approximated by a SET of boxes rather than one.

A sprite's silhouette is rarely a rectangle, and a single bounding box around
a diagonal or an L is mostly empty — a mover well clear of the art still reads
as a hit.  A handful of boxes tracks the silhouette closely enough to fix that
while staying axis-aligned, so every test below is still the cheap one.

The contract a producer owes is CONTAINMENT: every box together must cover
everything solid, so substituting the proxy for the art can only ever over-
report a hit, never miss one. A system validated against the proxy therefore
stays valid when the art changes. Containment alone is satisfied by a
screen-sized box, which is why a producer also bounds the OVERSHOOT — see
`overshoot`.

Measured over a 36-sprite corpus (@PLN146 F7a): 16 boxes banded along the
tighter axis beat a convex hull on mean, median and worst case, and need no
shape kind this library does not already have.

api.sig: pub fn proxy_hits(self: const Proxy, r: const Rect) -> boolean
api.doc:
Does anything in the proxy overlap `r`?

The set test every consumer would otherwise write, with the same STRICT
boundary as `rects_overlap` — a box sharing an edge does not overlap.  An
EMPTY proxy answers false: nothing solid was derived, so nothing can be hit,
which is the answer that keeps a sprite with no opaque texels from colliding
with the world.

api.sig: pub fn proxies_overlap(self: const Proxy, other: const Proxy) -> boolean
api.doc:
Do two proxies overlap anywhere?

Pairwise, because a proxy is small by construction — 16 boxes against 16 is
256 rect tests in the worst case and stops at the first hit.  Cull with the
cheap `bounds()` box first when both are large.

api.sig: pub fn bounds(self: const Proxy) -> Rect
api.doc:
The single box containing every box in the proxy — the AABB it replaces.

Useful as a broad-phase cull before `proxies_overlap`, and as the denominator
when judging whether the proxy earned its extra boxes.  An empty proxy answers
a zero-size box at the origin.

api.sig: pub fn area(self: const Proxy) -> float
api.doc:
Total area of the proxy's boxes.

Bands from one derivation do not overlap, so for a banded proxy this is the
covered area exactly.  A proxy whose boxes DO overlap counts the shared part
twice, which overstates the area and therefore the overshoot — the honest
direction for a bound.

`solid` is the area actually covered by art — the opaque texel count for a
sprite. `0.0` is exact, `1.0` is twice the size. This is the number a packer
gates on, and the reason containment alone is not the contract: a
screen-sized box contains everything and is useless.

to be a multiple OF, and a null here would propagate into a comparison that
then silently passes.

The trailing `?` is not redundant with that guard.  A divide types `float?`
whatever the code above it proves, so without the discharge this returns a
null into a non-null `float` — which is the very failure the guard is there to
prevent, arriving by the other door.

api.doc:

api.sig: pub struct ChunkField
pub fn field_new(layout: integer, xs: vector<integer>, ys: vector<integer>,
api.doc:
Build a field from placement-ordered coords.  The dirty index starts
empty; the spatial index (cidx) and the chunk->cell partition (buckets)
are built once (O(N)) and maintained incrementally thereafter
(field_add_cell), so a later collect_dirty_inputs is O(dirty), not O(N).

api.sig: pub fn field_add_cell(f: &ChunkField, x: integer, y: integer)
api.doc:
Edit — append a new cell (its index = old len(xs)), add it to its chunk's
bucket (O(1) amortised), and mark its chunk (+ halo-border neighbours)
dirty.  Keeping the bucket current here is what makes collect_dirty_inputs
O(dirty) rather than a full re-partition.

api.sig: pub fn field_mark_dirty(f: &ChunkField, x: integer, y: integer)
api.doc:
Edit — RECOLOUR an existing cell: mark its chunk (+ halo border) dirty
without touching the coord arrays or index (the cell stays; only its
consumer-side payload — colour/height — changed).  Erase uses
field_remove_cell instead (it must also drop the cell from the index).

api.sig: pub fn field_remove_cell(f: &ChunkField, x: integer, y: integer)
api.doc:
Edit — REMOVE an existing cell: drop it from the spatial index (cidx) and
its chunk bucket, then mark its chunk (+ halo border) dirty.  The MIRROR of
field_add_cell, sharing mark_borders so a removal flows through the IDENTICAL
incremental rebuild path as a paint.  The coord slot in xs/ys is deliberately
LEFT in place (not compacted): cell indices the field already handed out stay
stable, so a consumer's parallel per-cell arrays (e.g. the projector's bloom
births, indexed by cell index) are not invalidated.  The orphaned slot is
never read again — its index is in no bucket and no longer in cidx — and
re-painting the same coord allocates a FRESH index (field_add_cell appends),
so identity is never reused.

api.sig: pub fn clear_dirty(f: &ChunkField)
api.doc: Clear the dirty index after a rebuild (@P307 OpClearKeyed: in-place free).

api.sig: pub fn dirty_count(f: ChunkField) -> integer
api.doc: Number of chunks currently dirty (verification / O(dirty) sizing).

api.sig: pub fn chunk_is_dirty(f: ChunkField, x: integer, y: integer) -> boolean
api.doc: Is the chunk owning (x, y) currently marked dirty?

api.sig: pub struct ChunkInput
api.doc:
── B3: ChunkInput + per-chunk gather ─────────────────────────────────

What a per-cell RULE needs for ONE chunk: the indices of the cells it
OWNS (emit geometry for these) + the ≤halo_k border-neighbour cells in
OTHER chunks it may READ as context.  COMPACT — no payload, and NO copy
of the shared spatial index (`cidx`).  The rule receives `cidx`
SEPARATELY as a read-only ref (keyed params don't deep-copy) and `par`
forwards it as a context arg, so the per-chunk working set stays small
and cache-resident (copying the whole index per chunk would be O(N)).

api.sig: pub fn all_inputs(f: ChunkField, halo_k: integer) -> vector<ChunkInput>
api.doc:
One ChunkInput per chunk that holds cells (the full-build work-list).
Reads the wired-in `f.buckets` (no re-partition).

api.sig: pub fn collect_dirty_inputs(f: ChunkField, halo_k: integer) -> vector<ChunkInput>
api.doc:
One ChunkInput per DIRTY chunk (the incremental-rebuild work-list).
Iterates ONLY the dirty set and looks up each dirty chunk's bucket — so
the cost is O(dirty chunks × their cells), independent of total N.  A
dirty chunk with no owned cells (a halo-marked empty neighbour) is
skipped.  Clear the dirty index after rebuilding.

api.sig: pub struct GroupKey
pub struct GroupInput
api.doc:
The chunk ck's a group contains that actually hold cells (the assemble
work-list).  No mesh here — gridmesh partitions; the consumer owns meshes.

api.sig: pub fn group_of(cx: integer, cy: integer, group_dim: integer) -> GroupKey
api.doc:
The group owning CHUNK coord (cx, cy): chunk-space divided by group_dim.
Uses chunk_div so any group_dim works (not just powers of two) — a free dial.

api.sig: pub fn all_groups(f: ChunkField, group_dim: integer) -> vector<GroupInput>
api.doc:
One GroupInput per group that holds cells (the full-build work-list).
O(chunks): each non-empty chunk dedups into its group's chunk list.

api.sig: pub fn collect_dirty_groups(f: ChunkField, group_dim: integer) -> vector<GroupInput>
api.doc:
One GroupInput per DIRTY group (the incremental re-upload work-list).
A group is dirty if any of its chunks is dirty; its chunk_cks lists ALL its
member chunks that hold cells (so the consumer reassembles the group's VBO
from those chunks' CACHED meshes — unchanged chunks copied, not rebuilt).

FLAT COST: derives the dirty groups from f.dirty (O(dirty)), then for each
enumerates its group_dim × group_dim member chunk coords analytically and
probes f.buckets — O(dirty groups × group_dim²), independent of total N.
(Never scans all chunks, which would make per-edit cost grow with N.)

api.sig: pub fn all_groups(f: ChunkField, group_dim: integer) -> vector<GroupInput>
api.doc:
One GroupInput per group that holds cells (the full-build work-list).
O(chunks): each non-empty chunk dedups into its group's chunk list.

api.sig: pub fn collect_dirty_groups(f: ChunkField, group_dim: integer) -> vector<GroupInput>
api.doc:
One GroupInput per DIRTY group (the incremental re-upload work-list).
A group is dirty if any of its chunks is dirty; its chunk_cks lists ALL its
member chunks that hold cells (so the consumer reassembles the group's VBO
from those chunks' CACHED meshes — unchanged chunks copied, not rebuilt).

FLAT COST: derives the dirty groups from f.dirty (O(dirty)), then for each
enumerates its group_dim × group_dim member chunk coords analytically and
probes f.buckets — O(dirty groups × group_dim²), independent of total N.
(Never scans all chunks, which would make per-edit cost grow with N.)
Example: @GRM-004 — `chunk_cks` lists the group's CLEAN chunks too (copy their
cached meshes); reading it as "chunks to rebuild" rebuilds the whole group.

Loft integers are 64-bit signed post-2c, so the packed value fits
directly — no widening cast needed.

api.sig: pub fn rgba(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer, ca: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Pack RGBA channels into a single integer using bitwise ops.
Layout: bits 24..31 = alpha, 16..23 = red, 8..15 = green, 0..7 = blue.
Loft integers are 64-bit signed post-2c, so the packed value fits
directly — no widening cast needed.  Each channel is MASKED to 8 bits, so an
out-of-range argument wraps rather than saturating or being refused.
Example: @GFX-001 — the alpha byte is the one a hand-written hex literal
leaves at zero, and a zero alpha is fully transparent.

api.sig: pub fn rgb(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Opaque colour: the same pack with alpha 255.  `rgb(255, 0, 0)` is 0xFFFF0000 —
NOT the 0xFF0000 a reader reaches for, which has alpha 0.
Example: @GFX-001 — why the literal and this call are different colours, and
what each compositing path does with the difference.

api.sig: pub fn get_pixel(self: const Canvas, gx: integer, gy: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Get pixel color at (x, y). Returns 0 if out of bounds — and 0 is a COLOUR the
canvas can hold (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), so the answer cannot serve as a bounds
test.  Bound with `width`/`height`.
Example: @GFX-003 — a neighbourhood scan that tests the returned colour
miscounts its own transparent pixels as off-canvas.

api.sig: pub fn set_pixel(self: Canvas, sx: integer, sy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Set pixel color at (x, y). No-op if out of bounds.  STORES the colour byte for
byte, alpha included — it does not composite; `blend_pixel` does.
Example: @GFX-002 — storing a half-transparent colour replaces what was under
it, rather than showing through it.
Example: @GFX-003 — an out-of-range coordinate is declined in silence, so a
wrong index is a missing part of the drawing, never a message.

api.sig: pub fn clear(self: Canvas, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill the entire canvas with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn blend(dst: integer, src: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Alpha-blend src over dst. Both are 0xAARRGGBB packed integers.
Uses standard "src over" compositing: out = src * alpha + dst * (1 - alpha).

api.doc:
Draw a pixel with alpha blending at (x, y) — the compositing counterpart to

Example: @GFX-002 — store versus composite, side by side.

api.sig: pub fn fill_rect(self: Canvas, rx: integer, ry: integer, rw: integer, rh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a rectangle with a solid color. Clipped to canvas bounds.  Like every
solid primitive here it STORES the colour (see `set_pixel`); a rectangle drawn
in a half-transparent colour is not a translucent overlay.
Example: @GFX-002 — what the buffer holds afterwards.

api.sig: pub fn hline(self: Canvas, hx0: integer, hx1: integer, hy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a horizontal line from (x0, y) to (x1, y). Clipped.  The end is
EXCLUSIVE — `[x0, x1)` — and a reversed span draws nothing rather than being
normalised.
Example: @GFX-004 — where a span starts and stops, and what silence looks like.

api.sig: pub fn vline(self: Canvas, vx: integer, vy0: integer, vy1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a vertical line from (x, y0) to (x, y1). Clipped.  Exclusive end and
no normalisation, exactly like `hline`.
Example: @GFX-004 — the half-open span rule on both axes.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect(self: Canvas, drx: integer, dry: integer, drw: integer, drh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a rectangle outline (1px border). Clipped.  Built from four half-open
spans, so (x, y, w, h) covers x .. x + w - 1 by y .. y + h - 1.
Example: @GFX-004 — the exact pixels, and the hollow interior.

api.sig: pub fn draw_line(self: Canvas, lx0: integer, ly0: integer, lx1: integer, ly1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) using Bresenham's algorithm.
Handles all octants. Each pixel is set (no blending).

api.sig: pub fn draw_circle(self: Canvas, ccx: integer, ccy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a circle outline using the midpoint algorithm.
Center at (cx, cy) with the given radius. Clipped via set_pixel.

api.sig: pub fn fill_circle(self: Canvas, fcx: integer, fcy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill a circle (solid disk). Center at (cx, cy), given radius.

api.sig: pub fn fill_ellipse(self: Canvas, fex: integer, fey: integer, ferx: integer, fery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill an axis-aligned ellipse (solid). Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_ellipse(self: Canvas, ecx: integer, ecy: integer, erx: integer, ery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Draw an axis-aligned ellipse outline. Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_bezier(self: Canvas, bx0: integer, by0: integer, bx1: integer, by1: integer, bx2: integer, by2: integer, bx3: integer, by3: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a cubic Bezier curve from (bx0,by0) to (bx3,by3) with control points
(bx1,by1) and (bx2,by2). Uses adaptive subdivision — splits until segments
are flat enough, then draws with Bresenham lines.
Flatness threshold: max deviation of control points from the chord.

api.sig: pub fn draw_aa_line(self: Canvas, ax0: integer, ay0: integer, ax1: integer, ay1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw an anti-aliased line using Xiaolin Wu's algorithm.
Uses blend_pixel for sub-pixel coverage.

api.sig: pub fn fill_triangle(self: Canvas, tx0: integer, ty0: integer, tx1: integer, ty1: integer, tx2: integer, ty2: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a triangle with vertices (tx0,ty0), (tx1,ty1), (tx2,ty2).
Uses flat-top/flat-bottom decomposition with scanline fill.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Canvas, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Save canvas as a PNG file. Automatically uses RGBA if any pixel has alpha < 255,
otherwise uses RGB. Returns true on success.
Example: @GFX-005 — the choice is read off the pixels, so ONE alpha-0 pixel
(a hand-written hex literal — @GFX-001) makes the whole file RGBA and that
pixel a transparent hole.

api.sig: pub fn gl_screenshot(width: integer, height: integer, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Capture the current GL back-buffer to an RGB PNG.  Call after a frame's
draw calls and BEFORE gl_swap_buffers (reads GL_BACK).  Works on a
headless / Wayland desktop where the window itself can't be grabbed.

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_fullscreen(on: boolean)

Toggle fullscreen on the existing window (runtime flip, cheaper
than recreating the GL context — textures / VAOs / shaders
survive).  Pass `true` for borderless fullscreen, `false` for
windowed.  Browsers (WASM) require a user gesture to enter
fullscreen; calling outside one is non-fatal.

api.doc:
A 2D painter bundling shaders, a unit-quad VAO, and an orthographic

api.doc:
Draw a sprite from `sheet` at screen position (x, y) with size (w, h).
`sp_idx` is the 0-based sprite index (row-major) in the sheet.
This is a one-liner replacement for `make_mvp` + `draw_sprite`.

api.doc:
Draw an arbitrary GL texture as a screen-space quad at (x, y, w, h).

Suitable for textures created with `create_text_texture` or `gl_upload_canvas`.

api.sig: pub fn rgba(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer, ca: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Pack RGBA channels into a single integer using bitwise ops.
Layout: bits 24..31 = alpha, 16..23 = red, 8..15 = green, 0..7 = blue.
Loft integers are 64-bit signed post-2c, so the packed value fits
directly — no widening cast needed.  Each channel is MASKED to 8 bits, so an
out-of-range argument wraps rather than saturating or being refused.
Example: @GFX-001 — the alpha byte is the one a hand-written hex literal
leaves at zero, and a zero alpha is fully transparent.

api.sig: pub fn rgb(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Opaque colour: the same pack with alpha 255.  `rgb(255, 0, 0)` is 0xFFFF0000 —
NOT the 0xFF0000 a reader reaches for, which has alpha 0.
Example: @GFX-001 — why the literal and this call are different colours, and
what each compositing path does with the difference.

api.doc: Create a canvas filled with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn get_pixel(self: const Canvas, gx: integer, gy: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Get pixel color at (x, y). Returns 0 if out of bounds — and 0 is a COLOUR the
canvas can hold (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), so the answer cannot serve as a bounds
test.  Bound with `width`/`height`.
Example: @GFX-003 — a neighbourhood scan that tests the returned colour
miscounts its own transparent pixels as off-canvas.

api.sig: pub fn set_pixel(self: Canvas, sx: integer, sy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Set pixel color at (x, y). No-op if out of bounds.  STORES the colour byte for
byte, alpha included — it does not composite; `blend_pixel` does.
Example: @GFX-002 — storing a half-transparent colour replaces what was under
it, rather than showing through it.
Example: @GFX-003 — an out-of-range coordinate is declined in silence, so a
wrong index is a missing part of the drawing, never a message.

api.sig: pub fn clear(self: Canvas, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill the entire canvas with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn blend(dst: integer, src: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Alpha-blend src over dst. Both are 0xAARRGGBB packed integers.
Uses standard "src over" compositing: out = src * alpha + dst * (1 - alpha).

api.sig: pub fn blend_pixel(self: Canvas, bx: integer, by: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a pixel with alpha blending at (x, y) — the compositing counterpart to
`set_pixel`, and the one a caller reaching for alpha usually meant.
Example: @GFX-002 — store versus composite, side by side.

api.sig: pub fn fill_rect(self: Canvas, rx: integer, ry: integer, rw: integer, rh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a rectangle with a solid color. Clipped to canvas bounds.  Like every
solid primitive here it STORES the colour (see `set_pixel`); a rectangle drawn
in a half-transparent colour is not a translucent overlay.
Example: @GFX-002 — what the buffer holds afterwards.

api.sig: pub fn hline(self: Canvas, hx0: integer, hx1: integer, hy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a horizontal line from (x0, y) to (x1, y). Clipped.  The end is
EXCLUSIVE — `[x0, x1)` — and a reversed span draws nothing rather than being
normalised.
Example: @GFX-004 — where a span starts and stops, and what silence looks like.

api.sig: pub fn vline(self: Canvas, vx: integer, vy0: integer, vy1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a vertical line from (x, y0) to (x, y1). Clipped.  Exclusive end and
no normalisation, exactly like `hline`.
Example: @GFX-004 — the half-open span rule on both axes.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect(self: Canvas, drx: integer, dry: integer, drw: integer, drh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a rectangle outline (1px border). Clipped.  Built from four half-open
spans, so (x, y, w, h) covers x .. x + w - 1 by y .. y + h - 1.
Example: @GFX-004 — the exact pixels, and the hollow interior.

api.sig: pub fn draw_line(self: Canvas, lx0: integer, ly0: integer, lx1: integer, ly1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) using Bresenham's algorithm.
Handles all octants. Each pixel is set (no blending).

api.sig: pub fn draw_circle(self: Canvas, ccx: integer, ccy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a circle outline using the midpoint algorithm.
Center at (cx, cy) with the given radius. Clipped via set_pixel.

api.sig: pub fn fill_circle(self: Canvas, fcx: integer, fcy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill a circle (solid disk). Center at (cx, cy), given radius.

api.sig: pub fn fill_ellipse(self: Canvas, fex: integer, fey: integer, ferx: integer, fery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill an axis-aligned ellipse (solid). Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_ellipse(self: Canvas, ecx: integer, ecy: integer, erx: integer, ery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Draw an axis-aligned ellipse outline. Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_bezier(self: Canvas, bx0: integer, by0: integer, bx1: integer, by1: integer, bx2: integer, by2: integer, bx3: integer, by3: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a cubic Bezier curve from (bx0,by0) to (bx3,by3) with control points
(bx1,by1) and (bx2,by2). Uses adaptive subdivision — splits until segments
are flat enough, then draws with Bresenham lines.
Flatness threshold: max deviation of control points from the chord.

api.sig: pub fn draw_aa_line(self: Canvas, ax0: integer, ay0: integer, ax1: integer, ay1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw an anti-aliased line using Xiaolin Wu's algorithm.
Uses blend_pixel for sub-pixel coverage.

api.sig: pub fn fill_triangle(self: Canvas, tx0: integer, ty0: integer, tx1: integer, ty1: integer, tx2: integer, ty2: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a triangle with vertices (tx0,ty0), (tx1,ty1), (tx2,ty2).
Uses flat-top/flat-bottom decomposition with scanline fill.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Canvas, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Save canvas as a PNG file. Automatically uses RGBA if any pixel has alpha < 255,
otherwise uses RGB. Returns true on success.
Example: @GFX-005 — the choice is read off the pixels, so ONE alpha-0 pixel
(a hand-written hex literal — @GFX-001) makes the whole file RGBA and that
pixel a transparent hole.

api.sig: pub fn gl_screenshot(width: integer, height: integer, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Capture the current GL back-buffer to an RGB PNG.  Call after a frame's
draw calls and BEFORE gl_swap_buffers (reads GL_BACK).  Works on a
headless / Wayland desktop where the window itself can't be grabbed.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_window(width: integer, height: integer, title: text) -> boolean
api.doc: Create a window with an OpenGL 3.3 context. Returns true on success.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_fullscreen_window(title: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Open a borderless fullscreen window at the primary monitor's native
resolution. Returns true on success. Read the actual viewport size
afterwards with `gl_window_width` / `gl_window_height` if you need
to set up an aspect-aware camera.

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_fullscreen(on: boolean)
api.doc:
Toggle fullscreen on the existing window (runtime flip, cheaper
than recreating the GL context — textures / VAOs / shaders
survive).  Pass `true` for borderless fullscreen, `false` for
windowed.  Browsers (WASM) require a user gesture to enter
fullscreen; calling outside one is non-fatal.

api.sig: pub fn gl_window_width() -> integer
api.doc:
Current window inner size in physical pixels.  Query after creating a
(especially fullscreen) window so projection / 2D ortho / overlays use
the real resolution rather than a windowed hint.

api.sig: pub fn gl_window_height() -> integer
pub fn gl_poll_events() -> boolean
api.doc: Poll window events. Returns false when the window should close.

api.sig: pub fn gl_swap_buffers()
api.doc: Swap buffers (present the frame).

api.sig: pub fn gl_clear(color: integer)
api.doc: Clear the screen with an RGBA color (packed as 0xRRGGBBAA).

api.sig: pub fn gl_destroy_window()
api.doc: Destroy the window and OpenGL context.

api.doc: Compile and link a shader program. Returns the program ID (0 on failure).

api.sig: pub fn gl_use_shader(program: integer)
api.doc: Use a shader program for subsequent draw calls.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer)
api.doc: Draw a VAO with vertex_count vertices as triangles.

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_vertices(data: vector<single>, stride: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload a vector<single> as a vertex buffer. Returns VAO handle.
stride = floats per vertex (3=pos, 6=pos+normal, 10=pos+normal+color).
Native codegen: loft_gl_upload_vertices(data_ptr: *const f32, count: u32, stride: i32) -> i32

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_instance_buffer(data: vector<single>) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload per-instance data to a DYNAMIC_DRAW buffer. Returns the VBO handle
(pass it to gl_instance_attrib). DYNAMIC because instances change per frame.

api.sig: pub fn gl_instance_attrib(vao: integer, ivbo: integer, location: integer, components: integer, stride_floats: integer, offset_floats: integer)
api.doc:
Bind instance VBO `ivbo`'s field to attribute `location` on `vao`, advancing
once per INSTANCE (VertexAttribDivisor=1). components = floats in the field
(2=vec2, 4=vec4); stride_floats = floats per instance record; offset_floats =
this field's start within the record. Use locations >=5 to clear the vertex attrs.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_instanced(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer, instance_count: integer)
api.doc: Draw vertex_count vertices of `vao` as triangles, instance_count times.

api.sig: pub fn gl_update_buffer(vbo: integer, data: vector<single>)
api.doc:
Orphan + re-upload an existing VBO (returned by gl_upload_vertices /
gl_upload_instance_buffer) with new data, DYNAMIC_DRAW — per-frame updates
without recreating the buffer.

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_indices(vao: integer, data: vector<integer>) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload triangle indices as an element (index) buffer bound to `vao`, so
gl_draw_elements(vao, index_count, mode) draws indexed. Returns the EBO handle.

pub fn group_vbos_new(stride: integer, draw_mode: integer) -> GroupVboSet

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_framebuffer() -> integer
api.doc: Create a framebuffer object. Returns FBO handle.

api.doc: Create a depth-only texture for shadow mapping.

api.doc: Create an empty RGBA texture for render-to-texture.

Generate mipmaps + trilinear minification for `tex` (after its pixels are

api.doc:
Upload a sub-region of RGBA pixels (Canvas data, 0xAARRGGBB) into an existing
texture at (x,y) sized w*h — incremental atlas packing without re-uploading.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_fullscreen_quad()
api.doc:
Draw a fullscreen quad (for post-processing). Uses built-in VAO with UV coords.
Vertex shader receives: layout(location=0) vec2 aPos, layout(location=1) vec2 aUV.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_mode(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer, mode: integer)
api.doc: Draw a VAO with explicit mode (DRAW_TRIANGLES, DRAW_LINES, DRAW_POINTS).

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_elements(vao: integer, index_count: integer, mode: integer)
api.doc: Draw using an index buffer (EBO). mode: DRAW_TRIANGLES, DRAW_LINES, DRAW_POINTS.

api.doc: Set line width for DRAW_LINES rendering.

api.sig: pub fn gl_point_size(size: float)
api.doc: Set point size for DRAW_POINTS rendering.

api.sig: pub fn gl_key_pressed(key_code: integer) -> boolean
api.doc: Returns true if the key is currently pressed (use KEY_* constants).

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_x() -> float
api.doc: Mouse position X (pixels from left edge of window).

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_y() -> float
api.doc: Mouse position Y (pixels from top edge of window).

api.doc: Mouse button bitmask: 1=left, 2=right, 4=middle.

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_wheel() -> integer
api.doc:
Scroll-wheel delta accumulated since the last call (positive = up).
Reset on read.  Use per-frame to drive the editor's `InputState.in_wheel`
or any other scroll-driven UI.  Pixel-delta trackpad scrolling is

api.doc:
Pop the next queued input event and latch it; returns its EV_* tag, or

api.doc: Modifier bitmask of the latched event (MOD_SHIFT | MOD_CTRL | MOD_ALT | MOD_SUPER).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_repeat() -> boolean
api.doc: True if the latched key-down is an auto-repeat.

api.doc: UTF-8 text of the latched EV_TEXT event ("" otherwise).

api.doc: X position (pixels) of the latched mouse/touch event; width for EV_RESIZE.

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_y() -> float
api.doc: Y position (pixels) of the latched mouse/touch event; height for EV_RESIZE.

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_button() -> integer
api.doc: Button of the latched mouse event (1=left, 2=right, 4=middle).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_wheel() -> integer
api.doc: Wheel delta of the latched EV_WHEEL event (positive = up).

api.doc: Stable finger id of the latched EV_TOUCH_* event.

api.sig: pub fn gl_load_font(path: text) -> integer
api.doc:
Load a font from a file path. Returns a font handle (>= 0) or null on error.

#255: a RELATIVE path resolves against the program's OWN directory
(`source_dir()` — the source dir under `--interpret`, the executable's dir
under `--native`), so a bundled font travels with the program and loads
regardless of the launch directory (the symptom #255 hit: a font addressed
relative to the source missed under `--native`, which runs from a temp dir,
and text rendered invisible).  An ABSOLUTE path is used verbatim.  This
matches loft's program-relative file-I/O default (`file()` / `read_file`).

api.sig: pub fn gl_measure_text(font: integer, content: text, size: float) -> float
api.doc: Measure text width in pixels at the given font size.

api.sig: pub fn gl_text_height(font: integer, size: float) -> integer
api.doc: Return the line height in pixels for a font at the given size.

api.sig: pub fn gl_font_ascent(font: integer, size: float) -> float
api.doc:
@P340: return the font ASCENT in pixels (baseline -> top of glyphs) from the
font's real metrics.  gl_draw_text(x, y) anchors by the TOP, placing the
baseline at y + gl_font_ascent(font, size); to baseline-align mixed sizes,
draw each at y = baseline - gl_font_ascent(font, size_i).

pub fn gl_load_texture(path: text) -> integer
api.doc:
Load an image file (PNG, JPG) and upload it as a GL texture.
Returns the texture ID (0 on failure).

api.doc:
Upload Canvas pixel data as a GL texture. Returns the texture ID.

api.sig: pub struct SpriteSheet
api.doc:
A sprite sheet backed by a Canvas atlas uploaded as a GL texture.
Sprites are arranged in a grid of `ss_cols` x `ss_rows` cells.

api.sig: pub fn create_sprite_sheet(atlas: const Canvas, cols: integer, rows: integer, vao: integer) -> SpriteSheet
api.doc:
Create a sprite sheet from a Canvas atlas.
The canvas is divided into a grid of `cols` x `rows` cells.
Sprite index 0 is top-left, incrementing left-to-right then top-to-bottom.

api.sig: pub fn draw_sprite(sheet: const SpriteSheet, mvp: const vector<float>, sp_idx: integer)
api.doc:
Draw sprite at `index` (0-based, row-major).
`mvp` is the pre-multiplied projection * model matrix (16 singles).
The caller builds the MVP for the desired screen position and size.

api.sig: pub struct Painter2D
api.doc:
A 2D painter bundling shaders, a unit-quad VAO, and an orthographic
projection. Create once per window with `create_painter_2d`, then use
`draw_rect_at`, `draw_sprite_at`, and `draw_texture_at` to render.

api.sig: pub fn create_painter_2d(screen_w: float, screen_h: float) -> Painter2D
api.doc:
Create a Painter2D for a window of size `screen_w` x `screen_h`.
Compiles the flat and textured shaders, uploads the unit-quad VAO, and
builds an orthographic projection with the origin at the top-left.
Call once after `gl_create_window`.

api.sig: pub fn painter_vao(self: const Painter2D) -> integer
api.doc:
Return the unit-quad VAO owned by the painter, so it can be shared with
`create_sprite_sheet` instead of uploading a second copy.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect_at(painter: const Painter2D, x: float, y: float, w: float, h: float,
api.doc:
Draw a filled rectangle at screen position (x, y) with size (w, h).
Colour channels are in 0.0..1.0. Uses the painter's flat-color shader.

api.sig: pub fn draw_sprite_at(sheet: const SpriteSheet, painter: const Painter2D,
api.doc:
Draw a sprite from `sheet` at screen position (x, y) with size (w, h).
`sp_idx` is the 0-based sprite index (row-major) in the sheet.
This is a one-liner replacement for `make_mvp` + `draw_sprite`.

api.sig: pub fn draw_texture_at(painter: const Painter2D, tex: integer,
api.doc:
Draw an arbitrary GL texture as a screen-space quad at (x, y, w, h).
Uses the painter's textured shader, which flips V to match canvas origin.
Suitable for textures created with `create_text_texture` or `gl_upload_canvas`.

api.sig: pub fn create_text_texture(font: integer, content: text, size: float, color: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Rasterize `content` with `font` at `size` pixels, upload the glyph bitmap
as a GL texture, and return the texture ID. The texture is sized to fit
the measured text plus a small padding; pair with `draw_texture_at` to
render. Caller owns the texture — call `gl_delete_texture` when done.
Returns 0 if the text cannot be measured.

api.sig: pub fn rgba(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer, ca: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Pack RGBA channels into a single integer using bitwise ops.
Layout: bits 24..31 = alpha, 16..23 = red, 8..15 = green, 0..7 = blue.
Loft integers are 64-bit signed post-2c, so the packed value fits
directly — no widening cast needed.  Each channel is MASKED to 8 bits, so an
out-of-range argument wraps rather than saturating or being refused.
Example: @GFX-001 — the alpha byte is the one a hand-written hex literal
leaves at zero, and a zero alpha is fully transparent.

api.sig: pub fn rgb(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Opaque colour: the same pack with alpha 255.  `rgb(255, 0, 0)` is 0xFFFF0000 —
NOT the 0xFF0000 a reader reaches for, which has alpha 0.
Example: @GFX-001 — why the literal and this call are different colours, and
what each compositing path does with the difference.
