pub fn color_a(color: integer) -> integer
pub struct Canvas
pub fn canvas(cw: integer, ch: integer, fill_color: integer) -> Canvas
api.doc: Create a canvas filled with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn get_pixel(self: const Canvas, gx: integer, gy: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Get pixel color at (x, y). Returns 0 if out of bounds — and 0 is a COLOUR the
canvas can hold (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), so the answer cannot serve as a bounds
test.  Bound with `width`/`height`.
Example: @GFX-003 — a neighbourhood scan that tests the returned colour
miscounts its own transparent pixels as off-canvas.

api.sig: pub fn set_pixel(self: Canvas, sx: integer, sy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Set pixel color at (x, y). No-op if out of bounds.  STORES the colour byte for
byte, alpha included — it does not composite; `blend_pixel` does.
Example: @GFX-002 — storing a half-transparent colour replaces what was under
it, rather than showing through it.
Example: @GFX-003 — an out-of-range coordinate is declined in silence, so a
wrong index is a missing part of the drawing, never a message.

api.sig: pub fn clear(self: Canvas, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill the entire canvas with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn blend(dst: integer, src: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Alpha-blend src over dst. Both are 0xAARRGGBB packed integers.
Uses standard "src over" compositing: out = src * alpha + dst * (1 - alpha).

api.sig: pub fn blend_pixel(self: Canvas, bx: integer, by: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a pixel with alpha blending at (x, y) — the compositing counterpart to
`set_pixel`, and the one a caller reaching for alpha usually meant.
Example: @GFX-002 — store versus composite, side by side.

api.sig: pub fn fill_rect(self: Canvas, rx: integer, ry: integer, rw: integer, rh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a rectangle with a solid color. Clipped to canvas bounds.  Like every
solid primitive here it STORES the colour (see `set_pixel`); a rectangle drawn
in a half-transparent colour is not a translucent overlay.
Example: @GFX-002 — what the buffer holds afterwards.

api.sig: pub fn hline(self: Canvas, hx0: integer, hx1: integer, hy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a horizontal line from (x0, y) to (x1, y). Clipped.  The end is
EXCLUSIVE — `[x0, x1)` — and a reversed span draws nothing rather than being
normalised.
Example: @GFX-004 — where a span starts and stops, and what silence looks like.

api.sig: pub fn vline(self: Canvas, vx: integer, vy0: integer, vy1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a vertical line from (x, y0) to (x, y1). Clipped.  Exclusive end and
no normalisation, exactly like `hline`.
Example: @GFX-004 — the half-open span rule on both axes.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect(self: Canvas, drx: integer, dry: integer, drw: integer, drh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a rectangle outline (1px border). Clipped.  Built from four half-open
spans, so (x, y, w, h) covers x .. x + w - 1 by y .. y + h - 1.
Example: @GFX-004 — the exact pixels, and the hollow interior.

api.sig: pub fn draw_line(self: Canvas, lx0: integer, ly0: integer, lx1: integer, ly1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) using Bresenham's algorithm.
Handles all octants. Each pixel is set (no blending).

api.sig: pub fn draw_circle(self: Canvas, ccx: integer, ccy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a circle outline using the midpoint algorithm.
Center at (cx, cy) with the given radius. Clipped via set_pixel.

api.sig: pub fn fill_circle(self: Canvas, fcx: integer, fcy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill a circle (solid disk). Center at (cx, cy), given radius.

api.sig: pub fn fill_ellipse(self: Canvas, fex: integer, fey: integer, ferx: integer, fery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill an axis-aligned ellipse (solid). Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_ellipse(self: Canvas, ecx: integer, ecy: integer, erx: integer, ery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Draw an axis-aligned ellipse outline. Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_bezier(self: Canvas, bx0: integer, by0: integer, bx1: integer, by1: integer, bx2: integer, by2: integer, bx3: integer, by3: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a cubic Bezier curve from (bx0,by0) to (bx3,by3) with control points
(bx1,by1) and (bx2,by2). Uses adaptive subdivision — splits until segments
are flat enough, then draws with Bresenham lines.
Flatness threshold: max deviation of control points from the chord.

api.sig: pub fn draw_aa_line(self: Canvas, ax0: integer, ay0: integer, ax1: integer, ay1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw an anti-aliased line using Xiaolin Wu's algorithm.
Uses blend_pixel for sub-pixel coverage.

api.sig: pub fn fill_triangle(self: Canvas, tx0: integer, ty0: integer, tx1: integer, ty1: integer, tx2: integer, ty2: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a triangle with vertices (tx0,ty0), (tx1,ty1), (tx2,ty2).
Uses flat-top/flat-bottom decomposition with scanline fill.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Canvas, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Save canvas as a PNG file. Automatically uses RGBA if any pixel has alpha < 255,
otherwise uses RGB. Returns true on success.
Example: @GFX-005 — the choice is read off the pixels, so ONE alpha-0 pixel
(a hand-written hex literal — @GFX-001) makes the whole file RGBA and that
pixel a transparent hole.

api.sig: pub fn gl_screenshot(width: integer, height: integer, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Capture the current GL back-buffer to an RGB PNG.  Call after a frame's
draw calls and BEFORE gl_swap_buffers (reads GL_BACK).  Works on a
headless / Wayland desktop where the window itself can't be grabbed.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_window(width: integer, height: integer, title: text) -> boolean
api.doc: Create a window with an OpenGL 3.3 context. Returns true on success.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_fullscreen_window(title: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Open a borderless fullscreen window at the primary monitor's native
resolution. Returns true on success. Read the actual viewport size
afterwards with `gl_window_width` / `gl_window_height` if you need
to set up an aspect-aware camera.

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_fullscreen(on: boolean)
api.doc:
Toggle fullscreen on the existing window (runtime flip, cheaper
than recreating the GL context — textures / VAOs / shaders
survive).  Pass `true` for borderless fullscreen, `false` for
windowed.  Browsers (WASM) require a user gesture to enter
fullscreen; calling outside one is non-fatal.

api.sig: pub fn gl_window_width() -> integer
api.doc:
Current window inner size in physical pixels.  Query after creating a
(especially fullscreen) window so projection / 2D ortho / overlays use
the real resolution rather than a windowed hint.

api.sig: pub fn gl_window_height() -> integer
pub fn gl_poll_events() -> boolean
api.doc: Poll window events. Returns false when the window should close.

api.sig: pub fn gl_swap_buffers()
api.doc: Swap buffers (present the frame).

api.sig: pub fn gl_clear(color: integer)
api.doc: Clear the screen with an RGBA color (packed as 0xRRGGBBAA).

api.sig: pub fn gl_destroy_window()
api.doc: Destroy the window and OpenGL context.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_shader(vertex_source: text, fragment_source: text) -> integer
api.doc: Compile and link a shader program. Returns the program ID (0 on failure).

api.sig: pub fn gl_use_shader(program: integer)
api.doc: Use a shader program for subsequent draw calls.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer)
api.doc: Draw a VAO with vertex_count vertices as triangles.

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_vertices(data: vector<single>, stride: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload a vector<single> as a vertex buffer. Returns VAO handle.
stride = floats per vertex (3=pos, 6=pos+normal, 10=pos+normal+color).
Native codegen: loft_gl_upload_vertices(data_ptr: *const f32, count: u32, stride: i32) -> i32

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_instance_buffer(data: vector<single>) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload per-instance data to a DYNAMIC_DRAW buffer. Returns the VBO handle
(pass it to gl_instance_attrib). DYNAMIC because instances change per frame.

api.sig: pub fn gl_instance_attrib(vao: integer, ivbo: integer, location: integer, components: integer, stride_floats: integer, offset_floats: integer)
api.doc:
Bind instance VBO `ivbo`'s field to attribute `location` on `vao`, advancing
once per INSTANCE (VertexAttribDivisor=1). components = floats in the field
(2=vec2, 4=vec4); stride_floats = floats per instance record; offset_floats =
this field's start within the record. Use locations >=5 to clear the vertex attrs.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_instanced(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer, instance_count: integer)
api.doc: Draw vertex_count vertices of `vao` as triangles, instance_count times.

api.sig: pub fn gl_update_buffer(vbo: integer, data: vector<single>)
api.doc:
Orphan + re-upload an existing VBO (returned by gl_upload_vertices /
gl_upload_instance_buffer) with new data, DYNAMIC_DRAW — per-frame updates
without recreating the buffer.

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_indices(vao: integer, data: vector<integer>) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload triangle indices as an element (index) buffer bound to `vao`, so
gl_draw_elements(vao, index_count, mode) draws indexed. Returns the EBO handle.

api.sig: pub struct GroupVboSet
pub fn group_vbos_new(stride: integer, draw_mode: integer) -> GroupVboSet
api.doc: Create an empty set for a fixed vertex stride + draw mode.

api.sig: pub fn group_vbos_upsert(set: GroupVboSet, gk: integer, verts: vector<single>,
api.doc:
Upload (or RE-upload) one group's baked vertices: delete the group's old VAO
if present, upload the new data, and record the handle + vertex count + world
bounds.  Call this only for the DIRTY groups each edit; untouched groups keep
their cached VBOs.

api.sig: pub fn group_vbos_draw_all(set: GroupVboSet)
api.doc:
Draw every group's cached VBO with the set's draw mode.  (Per-group frustum
culling — skip groups whose world bounds fall outside the view — is a future
addition; the bounds are already stored.)

api.sig: pub fn group_vbos_destroy(set: GroupVboSet)
api.doc: Free every group's VAO and clear the set (call on teardown / world reset).

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_mat4(program: integer, name: text, mat: vector<float>)
api.doc:
Set a mat4 uniform on a shader program. mat is a Mat4.m vector (16 floats).
Native codegen: loft_gl_set_mat4(program: i32, name_ptr, name_len, mat_ptr: *const f64, count: u32)

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_float(program: integer, name: text, val: float)
api.doc: Set a float uniform.

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_int(program: integer, name: text, val: integer)
api.doc: Set an integer uniform (also used for sampler2D texture unit bindings).

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_vec2(program: integer, name: text, x: float, y: float)
api.doc: Set a vec2 uniform (e.g. screen size, texel size, a 2D offset).

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_vec3(program: integer, name: text, x: float, y: float, z: float)
api.doc: Set a vec3 uniform (e.g. light position, color).

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_vec4(program: integer, name: text, x: float, y: float, z: float, w: float)
api.doc: Set a vec4 uniform (e.g. an RGBA color, a rect x/y/w/h).

api.sig: pub fn gl_enable(cap: integer)
api.doc: Enable a GL capability (GL_DEPTH_TEST, GL_BLEND, GL_CULL_FACE, GL_SCISSOR_TEST).

api.sig: pub fn gl_disable(cap: integer)
api.doc: Disable a GL capability.

api.sig: pub fn gl_blend_func(src: integer, dst: integer)
api.doc: Set blend function (e.g. gl_blend_func(BLEND_SRC_ALPHA, BLEND_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)).

api.sig: pub fn gl_cull_face(face: integer)
api.doc: Set which face to cull (0=back, 1=front).

api.sig: pub fn gl_depth_mask(write: boolean)
api.doc: Enable/disable depth buffer writing.

api.sig: pub fn gl_viewport(x: integer, y: integer, w: integer, h: integer)
api.doc: Set the viewport rectangle (used for FBO render passes).

api.sig: pub fn gl_scissor(x: integer, y: integer, w: integer, h: integer)
api.doc:
Set the scissor box — clips rendering to this rect (origin bottom-left, like
the viewport). Takes effect only while gl_enable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST) is set; use
it for partial-damage redraw (re-render just a changed region).

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_framebuffer() -> integer
api.doc: Create a framebuffer object. Returns FBO handle.

api.sig: pub fn gl_bind_framebuffer(fbo: integer)
api.doc: Bind a framebuffer (0 = default screen framebuffer).

api.sig: pub fn gl_framebuffer_texture(fbo: integer, attachment: integer, tex: integer)
api.doc: Attach a texture to an FBO (attachment: 0=color, 1=depth).

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_depth_texture(width: integer, height: integer) -> integer
api.doc: Create a depth-only texture for shadow mapping.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_color_texture(width: integer, height: integer) -> integer
api.doc: Create an empty RGBA texture for render-to-texture.

api.sig: pub fn gl_texture_filter(tex: integer, nearest: boolean)
api.doc: Set a texture's filtering: nearest = crisp pixel-art, else linear/smooth.

api.sig: pub fn gl_generate_mipmap(tex: integer)
api.doc:
Generate mipmaps + trilinear minification for `tex` (after its pixels are
uploaded) — keeps minified sprites / atlas pages clean.

api.sig: pub fn gl_texture_subimage(tex: integer, x: integer, y: integer, w: integer, h: integer, data: vector<integer>)
api.doc:
Upload a sub-region of RGBA pixels (Canvas data, 0xAARRGGBB) into an existing
texture at (x,y) sized w*h — incremental atlas packing without re-uploading.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_fullscreen_quad()
api.doc:
Draw a fullscreen quad (for post-processing). Uses built-in VAO with UV coords.
Vertex shader receives: layout(location=0) vec2 aPos, layout(location=1) vec2 aUV.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_mode(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer, mode: integer)
api.doc: Draw a VAO with explicit mode (DRAW_TRIANGLES, DRAW_LINES, DRAW_POINTS).

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_elements(vao: integer, index_count: integer, mode: integer)
api.doc: Draw using an index buffer (EBO). mode: DRAW_TRIANGLES, DRAW_LINES, DRAW_POINTS.

api.sig: pub fn gl_line_width(width: float)
api.doc: Set line width for DRAW_LINES rendering.

api.sig: pub fn gl_point_size(size: float)
api.doc: Set point size for DRAW_POINTS rendering.

api.sig: pub fn gl_key_pressed(key_code: integer) -> boolean
api.doc: Returns true if the key is currently pressed (use KEY_* constants).

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_x() -> float
api.doc: Mouse position X (pixels from left edge of window).

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_y() -> float
api.doc: Mouse position Y (pixels from top edge of window).

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_button() -> integer
api.doc: Mouse button bitmask: 1=left, 2=right, 4=middle.

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_wheel() -> integer
api.doc:
Scroll-wheel delta accumulated since the last call (positive = up).
Reset on read.  Use per-frame to drive the editor's `InputState.in_wheel`
or any other scroll-driven UI.  Pixel-delta trackpad scrolling is
quantised at 20 px/line.

api.sig: pub fn gl_next_event() -> integer
api.doc:
Pop the next queued input event and latch it; returns its EV_* tag, or
EV_NONE when the queue is drained.  Call after gl_poll_events().

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_key() -> integer
api.doc: Named/keycode of the latched key event (the KEY_* constants).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_mods() -> integer
api.doc: Modifier bitmask of the latched event (MOD_SHIFT | MOD_CTRL | MOD_ALT | MOD_SUPER).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_repeat() -> boolean
api.doc: True if the latched key-down is an auto-repeat.

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_text() -> text
api.doc: UTF-8 text of the latched EV_TEXT event ("" otherwise).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_x() -> float
api.doc: X position (pixels) of the latched mouse/touch event; width for EV_RESIZE.

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_y() -> float
api.doc: Y position (pixels) of the latched mouse/touch event; height for EV_RESIZE.

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_button() -> integer
api.doc: Button of the latched mouse event (1=left, 2=right, 4=middle).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_wheel() -> integer
api.doc: Wheel delta of the latched EV_WHEEL event (positive = up).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_touch_id() -> integer
api.doc: Stable finger id of the latched EV_TOUCH_* event.

api.sig: pub fn gl_load_font(path: text) -> integer
api.doc:
Load a font from a file path. Returns a font handle (>= 0) or null on error.

#255: a RELATIVE path resolves against the program's OWN directory
(`source_dir()` — the source dir under `--interpret`, the executable's dir
under `--native`), so a bundled font travels with the program and loads
regardless of the launch directory (the symptom #255 hit: a font addressed
relative to the source missed under `--native`, which runs from a temp dir,
and text rendered invisible).  An ABSOLUTE path is used verbatim.  This
matches loft's program-relative file-I/O default (`file()` / `read_file`).

api.sig: pub fn gl_measure_text(font: integer, content: text, size: float) -> float
api.doc: Measure text width in pixels at the given font size.

api.sig: pub fn gl_text_height(font: integer, size: float) -> integer
api.doc: Return the line height in pixels for a font at the given size.

api.sig: pub fn gl_font_ascent(font: integer, size: float) -> float
api.doc:
@P340: return the font ASCENT in pixels (baseline -> top of glyphs) from the
font's real metrics.  gl_draw_text(x, y) anchors by the TOP, placing the
baseline at y + gl_font_ascent(font, size); to baseline-align mixed sizes,
draw each at y = baseline - gl_font_ascent(font, size_i).

api.sig: pub fn draw_text(self: Canvas, font: integer, content: text, size: float,
pub fn gl_load_texture(path: text) -> integer
api.doc:
Load an image file (PNG, JPG) and upload it as a GL texture.
Returns the texture ID (0 on failure).

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_canvas(data: vector<integer>, width: integer, height: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload Canvas pixel data as a GL texture. Returns the texture ID.
Converts 0xAARRGGBB packed integers to RGBA bytes for OpenGL.

api.sig: pub fn gl_bind_texture(texture_id: integer, unit: integer)
api.doc: Bind a texture to a texture unit (0-based) for rendering.

api.sig: pub fn gl_delete_texture(texture_id: integer)
api.doc: Delete a texture.

api.sig: pub fn gl_delete_shader(program: integer)
api.doc: Delete a shader program.

api.sig: pub fn gl_delete_vao(vao: integer)
api.doc: Delete a vertex array object.

api.sig: pub fn gl_delete_framebuffer(fbo: integer)
api.doc: Delete a framebuffer object.

api.sig: pub struct SpriteSheet
api.doc:
A sprite sheet backed by a Canvas atlas uploaded as a GL texture.
Sprites are arranged in a grid of `ss_cols` x `ss_rows` cells.

api.sig: pub fn create_sprite_sheet(atlas: const Canvas, cols: integer, rows: integer, vao: integer) -> SpriteSheet
api.doc:
Create a sprite sheet from a Canvas atlas.
The canvas is divided into a grid of `cols` x `rows` cells.
Sprite index 0 is top-left, incrementing left-to-right then top-to-bottom.

api.sig: pub fn draw_sprite(sheet: const SpriteSheet, mvp: const vector<float>, sp_idx: integer)
api.doc:
Draw sprite at `index` (0-based, row-major).
`mvp` is the pre-multiplied projection * model matrix (16 singles).
The caller builds the MVP for the desired screen position and size.

api.sig: pub struct Painter2D
api.doc:
A 2D painter bundling shaders, a unit-quad VAO, and an orthographic
projection. Create once per window with `create_painter_2d`, then use
`draw_rect_at`, `draw_sprite_at`, and `draw_texture_at` to render.

api.sig: pub fn create_painter_2d(screen_w: float, screen_h: float) -> Painter2D
api.doc:
Create a Painter2D for a window of size `screen_w` x `screen_h`.
Compiles the flat and textured shaders, uploads the unit-quad VAO, and
builds an orthographic projection with the origin at the top-left.
Call once after `gl_create_window`.

api.sig: pub fn painter_vao(self: const Painter2D) -> integer
api.doc:
Return the unit-quad VAO owned by the painter, so it can be shared with
`create_sprite_sheet` instead of uploading a second copy.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect_at(painter: const Painter2D, x: float, y: float, w: float, h: float,
api.doc:
Draw a filled rectangle at screen position (x, y) with size (w, h).
Colour channels are in 0.0..1.0. Uses the painter's flat-color shader.

api.sig: pub fn draw_sprite_at(sheet: const SpriteSheet, painter: const Painter2D,
api.doc:
Draw a sprite from `sheet` at screen position (x, y) with size (w, h).
`sp_idx` is the 0-based sprite index (row-major) in the sheet.
This is a one-liner replacement for `make_mvp` + `draw_sprite`.

api.sig: pub fn draw_texture_at(painter: const Painter2D, tex: integer,
api.doc:
Draw an arbitrary GL texture as a screen-space quad at (x, y, w, h).
Uses the painter's textured shader, which flips V to match canvas origin.
Suitable for textures created with `create_text_texture` or `gl_upload_canvas`.

api.sig: pub fn create_text_texture(font: integer, content: text, size: float, color: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Rasterize `content` with `font` at `size` pixels, upload the glyph bitmap
as a GL texture, and return the texture ID. The texture is sized to fit
the measured text plus a small padding; pair with `draw_texture_at` to
render. Caller owns the texture — call `gl_delete_texture` when done.
Returns 0 if the text cannot be measured.

api.sig: pub fn audio_load(path: text) -> integer
api.doc: Load an audio clip (WAV or OGG). Returns handle (>= 0) or null on failure.

api.sig: pub fn audio_play(clip: integer, volume: float) -> integer
api.doc: Play a loaded clip at the given volume (0.0-1.0). Returns playback handle.

api.sig: pub fn audio_stop(sink: integer)
api.doc: Stop a playing clip by its playback handle.

api.sig: pub fn audio_set_volume(sink: integer, volume: float)
api.doc: Set volume of a playing clip (0.0-1.0).

api.sig: pub fn audio_play_raw(samples: vector<single>, sample_rate: integer, volume: float) -> integer
api.doc:
Play raw PCM samples (mono, values -1.0 to 1.0) at the given sample rate.
Returns playback handle, or null on failure.

api.sig: pub fn sfx_beep(sb_freq: single, sb_dur: single, sb_vol: single) -> integer
api.doc: Short percussive beep — brick hit, UI click.

api.sig: pub fn sfx_descend(sd_f0: single, sd_f1: single, sd_dur: single, sd_vol: single) -> integer
api.doc: Descending tone — life lost, negative event.

api.sig: pub fn sfx_chirp(sc_f0: single, sc_f1: single, sc_dur: single, sc_vol: single) -> integer
api.doc: Rising chirp — pickup collected, positive event.

api.sig: pub fn sfx_noise(sn_dur: single, sn_vol: single) -> integer
api.doc: White noise burst — percussion, explosion, brick break.

api.sig: pub fn sfx_bounce(sp_freq: single, sp_vol: single) -> integer
api.doc: Paddle bounce — low square wave thud with pitch drop.

api.sig: pub struct Renderer
pub fn create_renderer(rw: integer, rh: integer, title: text) -> Renderer
api.doc:
Create a renderer with a window.  Compiles built-in shaders, allocates
shadow map FBO.  Returns null on failure (no display).

api.sig: pub fn elapsed(self: const Renderer) -> float
api.doc: Seconds since the renderer was created.

api.sig: pub fn upload_scene(self: Renderer, sc: const scene::Scene)
api.doc: Upload all meshes in the scene to GPU VAOs.

api.sig: pub fn render_frame_no_swap(self: Renderer, sc: const scene::Scene,
api.doc:
Render one frame's 3D passes WITHOUT swapping buffers.  Callers
that want to draw a 2D overlay between the 3D pass and the swap
(e.g. the native Moros editor's panel) use this variant and
invoke `graphics::gl_swap_buffers()` themselves after their
overlay renders.  Returns false when close requested.

Introduced by Initiative 03 Phase 3b (native moros editor
panel overlay).  The existing `render_frame` wrapper below
preserves backward compatibility with every current caller.

api.sig: pub fn render_frame(self: Renderer, sc: const scene::Scene,
api.doc:
Render one frame (3D passes + buffer swap).  Convenience wrapper
for callers that don't need a 2D overlay between the 3D pass and
the swap — brick-buster, 24-renderer-demo, and every other current
consumer.  Returns false when close requested.

api.sig: pub fn render_loop(self: Renderer, sc: const scene::Scene, cam: const scene::Camera)
api.doc: Convenience: render loop until close.

api.sig: pub fn destroy(self: Renderer)
api.doc: Destroy GPU resources and close the window.

api.sig: pub fn rgba(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer, ca: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Pack RGBA channels into a single integer using bitwise ops.
Layout: bits 24..31 = alpha, 16..23 = red, 8..15 = green, 0..7 = blue.
Loft integers are 64-bit signed post-2c, so the packed value fits
directly — no widening cast needed.  Each channel is MASKED to 8 bits, so an
out-of-range argument wraps rather than saturating or being refused.
Example: @GFX-001 — the alpha byte is the one a hand-written hex literal
leaves at zero, and a zero alpha is fully transparent.

api.sig: pub fn rgb(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Opaque colour: the same pack with alpha 255.  `rgb(255, 0, 0)` is 0xFFFF0000 —
NOT the 0xFF0000 a reader reaches for, which has alpha 0.
Example: @GFX-001 — why the literal and this call are different colours, and
what each compositing path does with the difference.

api.sig: pub fn color_r(color: integer) -> integer
pub fn color_g(color: integer) -> integer
pub fn color_b(color: integer) -> integer
pub fn color_a(color: integer) -> integer
pub struct Canvas
pub fn canvas(cw: integer, ch: integer, fill_color: integer) -> Canvas
api.doc: Create a canvas filled with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn get_pixel(self: const Canvas, gx: integer, gy: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Get pixel color at (x, y). Returns 0 if out of bounds — and 0 is a COLOUR the
canvas can hold (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), so the answer cannot serve as a bounds
test.  Bound with `width`/`height`.
Example: @GFX-003 — a neighbourhood scan that tests the returned colour
miscounts its own transparent pixels as off-canvas.

api.sig: pub fn set_pixel(self: Canvas, sx: integer, sy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Set pixel color at (x, y). No-op if out of bounds.  STORES the colour byte for
byte, alpha included — it does not composite; `blend_pixel` does.
Example: @GFX-002 — storing a half-transparent colour replaces what was under
it, rather than showing through it.
Example: @GFX-003 — an out-of-range coordinate is declined in silence, so a
wrong index is a missing part of the drawing, never a message.

api.sig: pub fn clear(self: Canvas, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill the entire canvas with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn blend(dst: integer, src: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Alpha-blend src over dst. Both are 0xAARRGGBB packed integers.
Uses standard "src over" compositing: out = src * alpha + dst * (1 - alpha).

api.sig: pub fn blend_pixel(self: Canvas, bx: integer, by: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a pixel with alpha blending at (x, y) — the compositing counterpart to
`set_pixel`, and the one a caller reaching for alpha usually meant.
Example: @GFX-002 — store versus composite, side by side.

api.sig: pub fn fill_rect(self: Canvas, rx: integer, ry: integer, rw: integer, rh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a rectangle with a solid color. Clipped to canvas bounds.  Like every
solid primitive here it STORES the colour (see `set_pixel`); a rectangle drawn
in a half-transparent colour is not a translucent overlay.
Example: @GFX-002 — what the buffer holds afterwards.

api.sig: pub fn hline(self: Canvas, hx0: integer, hx1: integer, hy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a horizontal line from (x0, y) to (x1, y). Clipped.  The end is
EXCLUSIVE — `[x0, x1)` — and a reversed span draws nothing rather than being
normalised.
Example: @GFX-004 — where a span starts and stops, and what silence looks like.

api.sig: pub fn vline(self: Canvas, vx: integer, vy0: integer, vy1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a vertical line from (x, y0) to (x, y1). Clipped.  Exclusive end and
no normalisation, exactly like `hline`.
Example: @GFX-004 — the half-open span rule on both axes.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect(self: Canvas, drx: integer, dry: integer, drw: integer, drh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a rectangle outline (1px border). Clipped.  Built from four half-open
spans, so (x, y, w, h) covers x .. x + w - 1 by y .. y + h - 1.
Example: @GFX-004 — the exact pixels, and the hollow interior.

api.sig: pub fn draw_line(self: Canvas, lx0: integer, ly0: integer, lx1: integer, ly1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) using Bresenham's algorithm.
Handles all octants. Each pixel is set (no blending).

api.sig: pub fn draw_circle(self: Canvas, ccx: integer, ccy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a circle outline using the midpoint algorithm.
Center at (cx, cy) with the given radius. Clipped via set_pixel.

api.sig: pub fn fill_circle(self: Canvas, fcx: integer, fcy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill a circle (solid disk). Center at (cx, cy), given radius.

api.sig: pub fn fill_ellipse(self: Canvas, fex: integer, fey: integer, ferx: integer, fery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill an axis-aligned ellipse (solid). Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_ellipse(self: Canvas, ecx: integer, ecy: integer, erx: integer, ery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Draw an axis-aligned ellipse outline. Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_bezier(self: Canvas, bx0: integer, by0: integer, bx1: integer, by1: integer, bx2: integer, by2: integer, bx3: integer, by3: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a cubic Bezier curve from (bx0,by0) to (bx3,by3) with control points
(bx1,by1) and (bx2,by2). Uses adaptive subdivision — splits until segments
are flat enough, then draws with Bresenham lines.
Flatness threshold: max deviation of control points from the chord.

api.sig: pub fn draw_aa_line(self: Canvas, ax0: integer, ay0: integer, ax1: integer, ay1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw an anti-aliased line using Xiaolin Wu's algorithm.
Uses blend_pixel for sub-pixel coverage.

api.sig: pub fn fill_triangle(self: Canvas, tx0: integer, ty0: integer, tx1: integer, ty1: integer, tx2: integer, ty2: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a triangle with vertices (tx0,ty0), (tx1,ty1), (tx2,ty2).
Uses flat-top/flat-bottom decomposition with scanline fill.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Canvas, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Save canvas as a PNG file. Automatically uses RGBA if any pixel has alpha < 255,
otherwise uses RGB. Returns true on success.
Example: @GFX-005 — the choice is read off the pixels, so ONE alpha-0 pixel
(a hand-written hex literal — @GFX-001) makes the whole file RGBA and that
pixel a transparent hole.

api.sig: pub fn gl_screenshot(width: integer, height: integer, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Capture the current GL back-buffer to an RGB PNG.  Call after a frame's
draw calls and BEFORE gl_swap_buffers (reads GL_BACK).  Works on a
headless / Wayland desktop where the window itself can't be grabbed.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_window(width: integer, height: integer, title: text) -> boolean
api.doc: Create a window with an OpenGL 3.3 context. Returns true on success.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_fullscreen_window(title: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Open a borderless fullscreen window at the primary monitor's native
resolution. Returns true on success. Read the actual viewport size
afterwards with `gl_window_width` / `gl_window_height` if you need
to set up an aspect-aware camera.

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_fullscreen(on: boolean)
api.doc:
Toggle fullscreen on the existing window (runtime flip, cheaper
than recreating the GL context — textures / VAOs / shaders
survive).  Pass `true` for borderless fullscreen, `false` for
windowed.  Browsers (WASM) require a user gesture to enter
fullscreen; calling outside one is non-fatal.

api.sig: pub fn gl_window_width() -> integer
api.doc:
Current window inner size in physical pixels.  Query after creating a
(especially fullscreen) window so projection / 2D ortho / overlays use
the real resolution rather than a windowed hint.

api.sig: pub fn gl_window_height() -> integer
pub fn gl_poll_events() -> boolean
api.doc: Poll window events. Returns false when the window should close.

api.sig: pub fn gl_swap_buffers()
api.doc: Swap buffers (present the frame).

api.sig: pub fn gl_clear(color: integer)
api.doc: Clear the screen with an RGBA color (packed as 0xRRGGBBAA).

api.sig: pub fn gl_destroy_window()
api.doc: Destroy the window and OpenGL context.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_shader(vertex_source: text, fragment_source: text) -> integer
api.doc: Compile and link a shader program. Returns the program ID (0 on failure).

api.sig: pub fn gl_use_shader(program: integer)
api.doc: Use a shader program for subsequent draw calls.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer)
api.doc: Draw a VAO with vertex_count vertices as triangles.

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_vertices(data: vector<single>, stride: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload a vector<single> as a vertex buffer. Returns VAO handle.
stride = floats per vertex (3=pos, 6=pos+normal, 10=pos+normal+color).
Native codegen: loft_gl_upload_vertices(data_ptr: *const f32, count: u32, stride: i32) -> i32

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_instance_buffer(data: vector<single>) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload per-instance data to a DYNAMIC_DRAW buffer. Returns the VBO handle
(pass it to gl_instance_attrib). DYNAMIC because instances change per frame.

api.sig: pub fn gl_instance_attrib(vao: integer, ivbo: integer, location: integer, components: integer, stride_floats: integer, offset_floats: integer)
api.doc:
Bind instance VBO `ivbo`'s field to attribute `location` on `vao`, advancing
once per INSTANCE (VertexAttribDivisor=1). components = floats in the field
(2=vec2, 4=vec4); stride_floats = floats per instance record; offset_floats =
this field's start within the record. Use locations >=5 to clear the vertex attrs.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_instanced(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer, instance_count: integer)
api.doc: Draw vertex_count vertices of `vao` as triangles, instance_count times.

api.sig: pub fn gl_update_buffer(vbo: integer, data: vector<single>)
api.doc:
Orphan + re-upload an existing VBO (returned by gl_upload_vertices /
gl_upload_instance_buffer) with new data, DYNAMIC_DRAW — per-frame updates
without recreating the buffer.

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_indices(vao: integer, data: vector<integer>) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload triangle indices as an element (index) buffer bound to `vao`, so
gl_draw_elements(vao, index_count, mode) draws indexed. Returns the EBO handle.

api.sig: pub struct GroupVboSet
pub fn group_vbos_new(stride: integer, draw_mode: integer) -> GroupVboSet
api.doc: Create an empty set for a fixed vertex stride + draw mode.

api.sig: pub fn group_vbos_upsert(set: GroupVboSet, gk: integer, verts: vector<single>,
api.doc:
Upload (or RE-upload) one group's baked vertices: delete the group's old VAO
if present, upload the new data, and record the handle + vertex count + world
bounds.  Call this only for the DIRTY groups each edit; untouched groups keep
their cached VBOs.

api.sig: pub fn group_vbos_draw_all(set: GroupVboSet)
api.doc:
Draw every group's cached VBO with the set's draw mode.  (Per-group frustum
culling — skip groups whose world bounds fall outside the view — is a future
addition; the bounds are already stored.)

api.sig: pub fn group_vbos_destroy(set: GroupVboSet)
api.doc: Free every group's VAO and clear the set (call on teardown / world reset).

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_mat4(program: integer, name: text, mat: vector<float>)

Native codegen: loft_gl_set_mat4(program: i32, name_ptr, name_len, mat_ptr: *const f64, count: u32)

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_float(program: integer, name: text, val: float)
api.doc: Set a float uniform.

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_int(program: integer, name: text, val: integer)
api.doc: Set an integer uniform (also used for sampler2D texture unit bindings).

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_vec2(program: integer, name: text, x: float, y: float)

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_vec3(program: integer, name: text, x: float, y: float, z: float)

api.sig: pub fn gl_set_uniform_vec4(program: integer, name: text, x: float, y: float, z: float, w: float)
api.doc: Set a vec4 uniform (e.g. an RGBA color, a rect x/y/w/h).

api.sig: pub fn gl_enable(cap: integer)
api.doc: Enable a GL capability (GL_DEPTH_TEST, GL_BLEND, GL_CULL_FACE, GL_SCISSOR_TEST).

api.sig: pub fn gl_disable(cap: integer)
api.doc: Disable a GL capability.

api.sig: pub fn gl_blend_func(src: integer, dst: integer)

api.sig: pub fn gl_cull_face(face: integer)

api.sig: pub fn gl_finish()
api.doc:
Block until every GL command issued so far has completed.

The call that makes a read-back trustworthy: `gl_screenshot` and any other
framebuffer read otherwise race the driver, so the same program can produce a
complete frame or an empty one from run to run.  Costs a stall by definition —
use it in a test or a screenshot path, never in a frame loop.

api.sig: pub fn gl_viewport(x: integer, y: integer, w: integer, h: integer)
api.doc: Set the viewport rectangle (used for FBO render passes).

api.sig: pub fn gl_scissor(x: integer, y: integer, w: integer, h: integer)
api.doc:
Set the scissor box — clips rendering to this rect (origin bottom-left, like
the viewport). Takes effect only while gl_enable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST) is set; use
it for partial-damage redraw (re-render just a changed region).

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_framebuffer() -> integer
api.doc: Create a framebuffer object. Returns FBO handle.

api.sig: pub fn gl_bind_framebuffer(fbo: integer)
api.doc: Bind a framebuffer (0 = default screen framebuffer).

api.sig: pub fn gl_framebuffer_texture(fbo: integer, attachment: integer, tex: integer)
api.doc: Attach a texture to an FBO (attachment: 0=color, 1=depth).

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_depth_texture(width: integer, height: integer) -> integer
api.doc: Create a depth-only texture for shadow mapping.

api.sig: pub fn gl_create_color_texture(width: integer, height: integer) -> integer
api.doc: Create an empty RGBA texture for render-to-texture.

api.sig: pub fn gl_texture_filter(tex: integer, nearest: boolean)
api.doc: Set a texture's filtering: nearest = crisp pixel-art, else linear/smooth.

api.sig: pub fn gl_generate_mipmap(tex: integer)
api.doc:
Generate mipmaps + trilinear minification for `tex` (after its pixels are
uploaded) — keeps minified sprites / atlas pages clean.

api.sig: pub fn gl_texture_subimage(tex: integer, x: integer, y: integer, w: integer, h: integer, data: vector<integer>)
api.doc:
Upload a sub-region of RGBA pixels (Canvas data, 0xAARRGGBB) into an existing
texture at (x,y) sized w*h — incremental atlas packing without re-uploading.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_fullscreen_quad()
api.doc:
Draw a fullscreen quad (for post-processing). Uses built-in VAO with UV coords.
Vertex shader receives: layout(location=0) vec2 aPos, layout(location=1) vec2 aUV.

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_mode(vao: integer, vertex_count: integer, mode: integer)
api.doc: Draw a VAO with explicit mode (DRAW_TRIANGLES, DRAW_LINES, DRAW_POINTS).

api.sig: pub fn gl_draw_elements(vao: integer, index_count: integer, mode: integer)
api.doc: Draw using an index buffer (EBO). mode: DRAW_TRIANGLES, DRAW_LINES, DRAW_POINTS.

api.sig: pub fn gl_line_width(width: float)
api.doc: Set line width for DRAW_LINES rendering.

api.sig: pub fn gl_point_size(size: float)
api.doc: Set point size for DRAW_POINTS rendering.

api.sig: pub fn gl_key_pressed(key_code: integer) -> boolean
api.doc: Returns true if the key is currently pressed (use KEY_* constants).

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_x() -> float
api.doc: Mouse position X (pixels from left edge of window).

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_y() -> float
api.doc: Mouse position Y (pixels from top edge of window).

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_button() -> integer
api.doc: Mouse button bitmask: 1=left, 2=right, 4=middle.

api.sig: pub fn gl_mouse_wheel() -> integer
api.doc:
Scroll-wheel delta accumulated since the last call (positive = up).
Reset on read.  Use per-frame to drive the editor's `InputState.in_wheel`
or any other scroll-driven UI.  Pixel-delta trackpad scrolling is
quantised at 20 px/line.

api.sig: pub fn gl_next_event() -> integer
api.doc:
Pop the next queued input event and latch it; returns its EV_* tag, or
EV_NONE when the queue is drained.  Call after gl_poll_events().

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_key() -> integer
api.doc: Named/keycode of the latched key event (the KEY_* constants).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_mods() -> integer
api.doc: Modifier bitmask of the latched event (MOD_SHIFT | MOD_CTRL | MOD_ALT | MOD_SUPER).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_repeat() -> boolean
api.doc: True if the latched key-down is an auto-repeat.

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_text() -> text
api.doc: UTF-8 text of the latched EV_TEXT event ("" otherwise).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_x() -> float
api.doc: X position (pixels) of the latched mouse/touch event; width for EV_RESIZE.

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_y() -> float
api.doc: Y position (pixels) of the latched mouse/touch event; height for EV_RESIZE.

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_button() -> integer
api.doc: Button of the latched mouse event (1=left, 2=right, 4=middle).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_wheel() -> integer
api.doc: Wheel delta of the latched EV_WHEEL event (positive = up).

api.sig: pub fn gl_event_touch_id() -> integer
api.doc: Stable finger id of the latched EV_TOUCH_* event.

api.sig: pub fn gl_load_font(path: text) -> integer
api.doc:
Load a font from a file path. Returns a font handle (>= 0) or null on error.

#255: a RELATIVE path resolves against the program's OWN directory
(`source_dir()` — the source dir under `--interpret`, the executable's dir
under `--native`), so a bundled font travels with the program and loads
regardless of the launch directory (the symptom #255 hit: a font addressed
relative to the source missed under `--native`, which runs from a temp dir,
and text rendered invisible).  An ABSOLUTE path is used verbatim.  This
matches loft's program-relative file-I/O default (`file()` / `read_file`).

api.sig: pub fn gl_measure_text(font: integer, content: text, size: float) -> float
api.doc: Measure text width in pixels at the given font size.

api.sig: pub fn gl_text_height(font: integer, size: float) -> integer
api.doc: Return the line height in pixels for a font at the given size.

api.sig: pub fn gl_font_ascent(font: integer, size: float) -> float
api.doc:
@P340: return the font ASCENT in pixels (baseline -> top of glyphs) from the
font's real metrics.  gl_draw_text(x, y) anchors by the TOP, placing the
baseline at y + gl_font_ascent(font, size); to baseline-align mixed sizes,
draw each at y = baseline - gl_font_ascent(font, size_i).

api.sig: pub fn draw_text(self: Canvas, font: integer, content: text, size: float,
pub fn gl_load_texture(path: text) -> integer
api.doc:
Load an image file (PNG, JPG) and upload it as a GL texture.
Returns the texture ID (0 on failure).

api.sig: pub fn gl_upload_canvas(data: vector<integer>, width: integer, height: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Upload Canvas pixel data as a GL texture. Returns the texture ID.

api.sig: pub fn gl_bind_texture(texture_id: integer, unit: integer)
api.doc: Bind a texture to a texture unit (0-based) for rendering.

api.sig: pub struct SpriteSheet
api.doc:
A sprite sheet backed by a Canvas atlas uploaded as a GL texture.
Sprites are arranged in a grid of `ss_cols` x `ss_rows` cells.

api.sig: pub fn create_sprite_sheet(atlas: const Canvas, cols: integer, rows: integer, vao: integer) -> SpriteSheet
api.doc:
Create a sprite sheet from a Canvas atlas.
The canvas is divided into a grid of `cols` x `rows` cells.
Sprite index 0 is top-left, incrementing left-to-right then top-to-bottom.

api.sig: pub fn draw_sprite(sheet: const SpriteSheet, mvp: const vector<float>, sp_idx: integer)
api.doc:
Draw sprite at `index` (0-based, row-major).
`mvp` is the pre-multiplied projection * model matrix (16 singles).
The caller builds the MVP for the desired screen position and size.

api.sig: pub struct Painter2D
api.doc:
A 2D painter bundling shaders, a unit-quad VAO, and an orthographic
projection. Create once per window with `create_painter_2d`, then use
`draw_rect_at`, `draw_sprite_at`, and `draw_texture_at` to render.

api.sig: pub fn create_painter_2d(screen_w: float, screen_h: float) -> Painter2D
api.doc:
Create a Painter2D for a window of size `screen_w` x `screen_h`.
Compiles the flat and textured shaders, uploads the unit-quad VAO, and
builds an orthographic projection with the origin at the top-left.
Call once after `gl_create_window`.

api.sig: pub fn painter_vao(self: const Painter2D) -> integer
api.doc:
Return the unit-quad VAO owned by the painter, so it can be shared with
`create_sprite_sheet` instead of uploading a second copy.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect_at(painter: const Painter2D, x: float, y: float, w: float, h: float,
api.doc:
Draw a filled rectangle at screen position (x, y) with size (w, h).
Colour channels are in 0.0..1.0. Uses the painter's flat-color shader.

api.sig: pub fn draw_sprite_at(sheet: const SpriteSheet, painter: const Painter2D,
api.doc:
Draw a sprite from `sheet` at screen position (x, y) with size (w, h).
`sp_idx` is the 0-based sprite index (row-major) in the sheet.
This is a one-liner replacement for `make_mvp` + `draw_sprite`.

api.sig: pub fn draw_texture_at(painter: const Painter2D, tex: integer,
api.doc:
Draw an arbitrary GL texture as a screen-space quad at (x, y, w, h).
Uses the painter's textured shader, which flips V to match canvas origin.
Suitable for textures created with `create_text_texture` or `gl_upload_canvas`.

api.sig: pub fn create_text_texture(font: integer, content: text, size: float, color: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Rasterize `content` with `font` at `size` pixels, upload the glyph bitmap
as a GL texture, and return the texture ID. The texture is sized to fit
the measured text plus a small padding; pair with `draw_texture_at` to
render. Caller owns the texture — call `gl_delete_texture` when done.
Returns 0 if the text cannot be measured.

Play raw PCM samples (mono, values -1.0 to 1.0) at the given sample rate.

api.doc: Short percussive beep — brick hit, UI click.

api.sig: pub fn sfx_chirp(sc_f0: single, sc_f1: single, sc_dur: single, sc_vol: single) -> integer

api.sig: pub struct Renderer
pub fn create_renderer(rw: integer, rh: integer, title: text) -> Renderer
api.doc:

api.sig: pub fn rgba(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer, ca: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Pack RGBA channels into a single integer using bitwise ops.
Layout: bits 24..31 = alpha, 16..23 = red, 8..15 = green, 0..7 = blue.
Loft integers are 64-bit signed post-2c, so the packed value fits
directly — no widening cast needed.  Each channel is MASKED to 8 bits, so an
out-of-range argument wraps rather than saturating or being refused.
Example: @GFX-001 — the alpha byte is the one a hand-written hex literal
leaves at zero, and a zero alpha is fully transparent.

api.sig: pub fn rgb(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Opaque colour: the same pack with alpha 255.  `rgb(255, 0, 0)` is 0xFFFF0000 —
NOT the 0xFF0000 a reader reaches for, which has alpha 0.
Example: @GFX-001 — why the literal and this call are different colours, and
what each compositing path does with the difference.

pub struct Canvas
pub fn canvas(cw: integer, ch: integer, fill_color: integer) -> Canvas
api.doc: Create a canvas filled with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn get_pixel(self: const Canvas, gx: integer, gy: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Get pixel color at (x, y). Returns 0 if out of bounds — and 0 is a COLOUR the
canvas can hold (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), so the answer cannot serve as a bounds
test.  Bound with `width`/`height`.
Example: @GFX-003 — a neighbourhood scan that tests the returned colour
miscounts its own transparent pixels as off-canvas.

api.sig: pub fn set_pixel(self: Canvas, sx: integer, sy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Set pixel color at (x, y). No-op if out of bounds.  STORES the colour byte for
byte, alpha included — it does not composite; `blend_pixel` does.
Example: @GFX-002 — storing a half-transparent colour replaces what was under
it, rather than showing through it.
Example: @GFX-003 — an out-of-range coordinate is declined in silence, so a
wrong index is a missing part of the drawing, never a message.

api.sig: pub fn clear(self: Canvas, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill the entire canvas with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn blend(dst: integer, src: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Alpha-blend src over dst. Both are 0xAARRGGBB packed integers.
Uses standard "src over" compositing: out = src * alpha + dst * (1 - alpha).

api.sig: pub fn blend_pixel(self: Canvas, bx: integer, by: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a pixel with alpha blending at (x, y) — the compositing counterpart to
`set_pixel`, and the one a caller reaching for alpha usually meant.
Example: @GFX-002 — store versus composite, side by side.

api.sig: pub fn fill_rect(self: Canvas, rx: integer, ry: integer, rw: integer, rh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a rectangle with a solid color. Clipped to canvas bounds.  Like every
solid primitive here it STORES the colour (see `set_pixel`); a rectangle drawn
in a half-transparent colour is not a translucent overlay.
Example: @GFX-002 — what the buffer holds afterwards.

api.sig: pub fn hline(self: Canvas, hx0: integer, hx1: integer, hy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a horizontal line from (x0, y) to (x1, y). Clipped.  The end is
EXCLUSIVE — `[x0, x1)` — and a reversed span draws nothing rather than being
normalised.
Example: @GFX-004 — where a span starts and stops, and what silence looks like.

api.sig: pub fn vline(self: Canvas, vx: integer, vy0: integer, vy1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a vertical line from (x, y0) to (x, y1). Clipped.  Exclusive end and
no normalisation, exactly like `hline`.
Example: @GFX-004 — the half-open span rule on both axes.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect(self: Canvas, drx: integer, dry: integer, drw: integer, drh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a rectangle outline (1px border). Clipped.  Built from four half-open
spans, so (x, y, w, h) covers x .. x + w - 1 by y .. y + h - 1.
Example: @GFX-004 — the exact pixels, and the hollow interior.

api.sig: pub fn draw_line(self: Canvas, lx0: integer, ly0: integer, lx1: integer, ly1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) using Bresenham's algorithm.
Handles all octants. Each pixel is set (no blending).

api.sig: pub fn draw_circle(self: Canvas, ccx: integer, ccy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a circle outline using the midpoint algorithm.
Center at (cx, cy) with the given radius. Clipped via set_pixel.

api.sig: pub fn fill_circle(self: Canvas, fcx: integer, fcy: integer, radius: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill a circle (solid disk). Center at (cx, cy), given radius.

api.sig: pub fn fill_ellipse(self: Canvas, fex: integer, fey: integer, ferx: integer, fery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill an axis-aligned ellipse (solid). Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_ellipse(self: Canvas, ecx: integer, ecy: integer, erx: integer, ery: integer, color: integer)
api.doc: Draw an axis-aligned ellipse outline. Center (cx, cy), radii (rx, ry).

api.sig: pub fn draw_bezier(self: Canvas, bx0: integer, by0: integer, bx1: integer, by1: integer, bx2: integer, by2: integer, bx3: integer, by3: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a cubic Bezier curve from (bx0,by0) to (bx3,by3) with control points
(bx1,by1) and (bx2,by2). Uses adaptive subdivision — splits until segments
are flat enough, then draws with Bresenham lines.
Flatness threshold: max deviation of control points from the chord.

api.sig: pub fn draw_aa_line(self: Canvas, ax0: integer, ay0: integer, ax1: integer, ay1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw an anti-aliased line using Xiaolin Wu's algorithm.
Uses blend_pixel for sub-pixel coverage.

api.sig: pub fn fill_triangle(self: Canvas, tx0: integer, ty0: integer, tx1: integer, ty1: integer, tx2: integer, ty2: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a triangle with vertices (tx0,ty0), (tx1,ty1), (tx2,ty2).
Uses flat-top/flat-bottom decomposition with scanline fill.

api.sig: pub struct Coord
api.doc:
A point on the canvas, in pixels.

Exists because a polygon is a LIST of them and `fill_triangle`'s six loose
integers do not generalise — six is already the edge of what a caller gets
right in order, and a polygon has no fixed count.

NOT called `Point`: `mesh3d::LightType` has a `Point` variant and `graphics`
depends on mesh3d, so the name is taken and the collision is a hard error
("struct 'Point' conflicts with a enumvalue of the same name"). `Vertex` is
mesh3d's too. Reach for `Coord` in 2-D graphics code and the 3-D names stay
where they belong.

api.sig: pub fn fill_polygon(self: Canvas, pts: const vector<Coord>, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a closed polygon under the EVEN-ODD rule.

The polygon closes itself: the last point joins the first, so a triangle is
three points and not four. Fewer than three points draws nothing.

Even-odd means a point is inside when a ray from it crosses the outline an odd
number of times, so a self-intersecting outline leaves its overlap EMPTY — the
classic five-point star is a pentagon-shaped hole with five filled arms. That
is a choice, not a bug: the alternative (non-zero winding) fills the middle,
and the two disagree on exactly the shapes people draw deliberately.

Matches `fill_triangle` pixel for pixel on a triangle, which is the reason the
row rule below is inclusive rather than the half-open rule a scanline filler
usually takes. See the note on `polygon_crossings`.
Example: @GFX-006 — the star's hollow middle, and the triangle agreement.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Canvas, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Save canvas as a PNG file. Automatically uses RGBA if any pixel has alpha < 255,
otherwise uses RGB. Returns true on success.
Example: @GFX-005 — the choice is read off the pixels, so ONE alpha-0 pixel
(a hand-written hex literal — @GFX-001) makes the whole file RGBA and that
pixel a transparent hole.

api.sig: pub fn gl_load_font(path: text) -> integer
api.doc:
Load a font from a file path. Returns a font handle (>= 0) or null on error.

#255: a RELATIVE path resolves against the program's OWN directory
(`source_dir()` — the source dir under `--interpret`, the executable's dir
under `--native`), so a bundled font travels with the program and loads
regardless of the launch directory (the symptom #255 hit: a font addressed
relative to the source missed under `--native`, which runs from a temp dir,
and text rendered invisible).  An ABSOLUTE path is used verbatim.  This
matches loft's program-relative file-I/O default (`file()` / `read_file`).

draw each at y = baseline - gl_font_ascent(font, size_i).

api.sig: pub struct Painter2D
api.doc:
A 2D painter bundling shaders, a unit-quad VAO, and an orthographic
projection. Create once per window with `create_painter_2d`, then use
`draw_rect_at`, `draw_sprite_at`, and `draw_texture_at` to render.

api.sig: pub fn create_painter_2d(screen_w: float, screen_h: float) -> Painter2D
api.doc:
Create a Painter2D for a window of size `screen_w` x `screen_h`.
Compiles the flat and textured shaders, uploads the unit-quad VAO, and
builds an orthographic projection with the origin at the top-left.
Call once after `gl_create_window`.

api.sig: pub fn painter_vao(self: const Painter2D) -> integer
api.doc:
Return the unit-quad VAO owned by the painter, so it can be shared with
`create_sprite_sheet` instead of uploading a second copy.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect_at(painter: const Painter2D, x: float, y: float, w: float, h: float,
api.doc:

api.sig: pub fn rgba(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer, ca: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Pack RGBA channels into a single integer using bitwise ops.
Layout: bits 24..31 = alpha, 16..23 = red, 8..15 = green, 0..7 = blue.
Loft integers are 64-bit signed post-2c, so the packed value fits
directly — no widening cast needed.  Each channel is MASKED to 8 bits, so an
out-of-range argument wraps rather than saturating or being refused.
Example: @GFX-001 — the alpha byte is the one a hand-written hex literal
leaves at zero, and a zero alpha is fully transparent.

api.sig: pub fn rgb(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Opaque colour: the same pack with alpha 255.  `rgb(255, 0, 0)` is 0xFFFF0000 —
NOT the 0xFF0000 a reader reaches for, which has alpha 0.
Example: @GFX-001 — why the literal and this call are different colours, and
what each compositing path does with the difference.

api.sig: pub fn get_pixel(self: const Canvas, gx: integer, gy: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Get pixel color at (x, y). Returns 0 if out of bounds — and 0 is a COLOUR the
canvas can hold (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), so the answer cannot serve as a bounds
test.  Bound with `width`/`height`.
Example: @GFX-003 — a neighbourhood scan that tests the returned colour
miscounts its own transparent pixels as off-canvas.

api.sig: pub fn set_pixel(self: Canvas, sx: integer, sy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Set pixel color at (x, y). No-op if out of bounds.  STORES the colour byte for
byte, alpha included — it does not composite; `blend_pixel` does.
Example: @GFX-002 — storing a half-transparent colour replaces what was under
it, rather than showing through it.
Example: @GFX-003 — an out-of-range coordinate is declined in silence, so a
wrong index is a missing part of the drawing, never a message.

api.sig: pub fn clear(self: Canvas, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill the entire canvas with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn blend(dst: integer, src: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Alpha-blend src over dst. Both are 0xAARRGGBB packed integers.
Uses standard "src over" compositing: out = src * alpha + dst * (1 - alpha).

api.doc:
Draw a pixel with alpha blending at (x, y) — the compositing counterpart to
`set_pixel`, and the one a caller reaching for alpha usually meant.
Example: @GFX-002 — store versus composite, side by side.

api.sig: pub fn fill_rect(self: Canvas, rx: integer, ry: integer, rw: integer, rh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a rectangle with a solid color. Clipped to canvas bounds.  Like every
solid primitive here it STORES the colour (see `set_pixel`); a rectangle drawn
in a half-transparent colour is not a translucent overlay.
Example: @GFX-002 — what the buffer holds afterwards.

api.sig: pub fn hline(self: Canvas, hx0: integer, hx1: integer, hy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a horizontal line from (x0, y) to (x1, y). Clipped.  The end is
EXCLUSIVE — `[x0, x1)` — and a reversed span draws nothing rather than being
normalised.
Example: @GFX-004 — where a span starts and stops, and what silence looks like.

api.sig: pub fn vline(self: Canvas, vx: integer, vy0: integer, vy1: integer, color: integer)

Draw a vertical line from (x, y0) to (x, y1). Clipped.  Exclusive end and
no normalisation, exactly like `hline`.
Example: @GFX-004 — the half-open span rule on both axes.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect(self: Canvas, drx: integer, dry: integer, drw: integer, drh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:

spans, so (x, y, w, h) covers x .. x + w - 1 by y .. y + h - 1.
Example: @GFX-004 — the exact pixels, and the hollow interior.

api.sig: pub fn fill_triangle(self: Canvas, tx0: integer, ty0: integer, tx1: integer, ty1: integer, tx2: integer, ty2: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a triangle with vertices (tx0,ty0), (tx1,ty1), (tx2,ty2).
Uses flat-top/flat-bottom decomposition with scanline fill.

api.sig: pub struct Coord
api.doc:
A point on the canvas, in pixels.

Exists because a polygon is a LIST of them and `fill_triangle`'s six loose
integers do not generalise — six is already the edge of what a caller gets
right in order, and a polygon has no fixed count.

NOT called `Point`: `mesh3d::LightType` has a `Point` variant and `graphics`
depends on mesh3d, so the name is taken and the collision is a hard error
("struct 'Point' conflicts with a enumvalue of the same name"). `Vertex` is
mesh3d's too. Reach for `Coord` in 2-D graphics code and the 3-D names stay
where they belong.

api.sig: pub fn fill_polygon(self: Canvas, pts: const vector<Coord>, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a closed polygon under the EVEN-ODD rule.

The polygon closes itself: the last point joins the first, so a triangle is
three points and not four. Fewer than three points draws nothing.

Even-odd means a point is inside when a ray from it crosses the outline an odd
number of times, so a self-intersecting outline leaves its overlap EMPTY — the
classic five-point star is a pentagon-shaped hole with five filled arms. That
is a choice, not a bug: the alternative (non-zero winding) fills the middle,
and the two disagree on exactly the shapes people draw deliberately.

Matches `fill_triangle` pixel for pixel on a triangle, which is the reason the
row rule below is inclusive rather than the half-open rule a scanline filler
usually takes. See the note on `polygon_crossings`.
Example: @GFX-006 — the star's hollow middle, and the triangle agreement.

api.sig: pub fn resize_lanczos(self: const Canvas, ow: integer, oh: integer) -> Canvas
api.doc:
Resample this canvas to `ow` x `oh` with a Lanczos-3 filter.

Byte-identical to Pillow's `Image.resize(..., Image.LANCZOS)`, which is the
point: the `.draw` corpus renders at 3x and downscales with exactly that, so a
renderer that resamples any other way cannot be pixel-compared against it
however good it looks (@PLN146 W0 finding 5).

**Alpha is premultiplied across the resample and undone after**, because
Pillow defines `resize` on an image with alpha as
`convert("RGBa") -> resize -> convert("RGBA")`. That is a contract, not an
optimisation: resampling straight RGBA lets a transparent texel's colour bleed
into its neighbours, and the two disagree on any edge where alpha varies.
Both roundings are Pillow's and neither is the obvious one — `(v*a + 127)/255`
going in, a TRUNCATING divide coming out, and alpha 0 passes its colour
through untouched rather than going black.
Example: @GFX-007 — why a 3x supersample plus this is not the same picture as
drawing once at final size.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Canvas, path: text) -> boolean

Save canvas as a PNG file. Automatically uses RGBA if any pixel has alpha < 255,

pixel a transparent hole.

regardless of the launch directory (the symptom #255 hit: a font addressed
relative to the source missed under `--native`, which runs from a temp dir,
and text rendered invisible).  An ABSOLUTE path is used verbatim.  This
matches loft's program-relative file-I/O default (`file()` / `read_file`).

api.sig: pub fn rgba(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer, ca: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Pack RGBA channels into a single integer using bitwise ops.
Layout: bits 24..31 = alpha, 16..23 = red, 8..15 = green, 0..7 = blue.
Loft integers are 64-bit signed post-2c, so the packed value fits
directly — no widening cast needed.  Each channel is MASKED to 8 bits, so an
out-of-range argument wraps rather than saturating or being refused.
Example: @GFX-001 — the alpha byte is the one a hand-written hex literal
leaves at zero, and a zero alpha is fully transparent.

api.sig: pub fn rgb(cr: integer, cg: integer, cb: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Opaque colour: the same pack with alpha 255.  `rgb(255, 0, 0)` is 0xFFFF0000 —
NOT the 0xFF0000 a reader reaches for, which has alpha 0.
Example: @GFX-001 — why the literal and this call are different colours, and
what each compositing path does with the difference.

api.doc: Create a canvas filled with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn get_pixel(self: const Canvas, gx: integer, gy: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Get pixel color at (x, y). Returns 0 if out of bounds — and 0 is a COLOUR the
canvas can hold (`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), so the answer cannot serve as a bounds
test.  Bound with `width`/`height`.
Example: @GFX-003 — a neighbourhood scan that tests the returned colour
miscounts its own transparent pixels as off-canvas.

api.sig: pub fn set_pixel(self: Canvas, sx: integer, sy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Set pixel color at (x, y). No-op if out of bounds.  STORES the colour byte for
byte, alpha included — it does not composite; `blend_pixel` does.
Example: @GFX-002 — storing a half-transparent colour replaces what was under
it, rather than showing through it.
Example: @GFX-003 — an out-of-range coordinate is declined in silence, so a
wrong index is a missing part of the drawing, never a message.

api.sig: pub fn clear(self: Canvas, color: integer)
api.doc: Fill the entire canvas with a solid color.

api.sig: pub fn blend(dst: integer, src: integer) -> integer
api.doc:
Alpha-blend src over dst. Both are 0xAARRGGBB packed integers.
Uses standard "src over" compositing: out = src * alpha + dst * (1 - alpha).

api.sig: pub fn blend_pixel(self: Canvas, bx: integer, by: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a pixel with alpha blending at (x, y) — the compositing counterpart to
`set_pixel`, and the one a caller reaching for alpha usually meant.
Example: @GFX-002 — store versus composite, side by side.

api.sig: pub fn fill_rect(self: Canvas, rx: integer, ry: integer, rw: integer, rh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a rectangle with a solid color. Clipped to canvas bounds.  Like every
solid primitive here it STORES the colour (see `set_pixel`); a rectangle drawn
in a half-transparent colour is not a translucent overlay.
Example: @GFX-002 — what the buffer holds afterwards.

api.sig: pub fn hline(self: Canvas, hx0: integer, hx1: integer, hy: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a horizontal line from (x0, y) to (x1, y). Clipped.  The end is
EXCLUSIVE — `[x0, x1)` — and a reversed span draws nothing rather than being
normalised.
Example: @GFX-004 — where a span starts and stops, and what silence looks like.

api.sig: pub fn vline(self: Canvas, vx: integer, vy0: integer, vy1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a vertical line from (x, y0) to (x, y1). Clipped.  Exclusive end and
no normalisation, exactly like `hline`.
Example: @GFX-004 — the half-open span rule on both axes.

api.sig: pub fn draw_rect(self: Canvas, drx: integer, dry: integer, drw: integer, drh: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a rectangle outline (1px border). Clipped.  Built from four half-open
spans, so (x, y, w, h) covers x .. x + w - 1 by y .. y + h - 1.
Example: @GFX-004 — the exact pixels, and the hollow interior.

api.sig: pub fn draw_line(self: Canvas, lx0: integer, ly0: integer, lx1: integer, ly1: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Draw a line from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) using Bresenham's algorithm.
Handles all octants. Each pixel is set (no blending).

api.doc:
Draw a circle outline using the midpoint algorithm.

api.sig: pub fn draw_bezier(self: Canvas, bx0: integer, by0: integer, bx1: integer, by1: integer, bx2: integer, by2: integer, bx3: integer, by3: integer, color: integer)

api.sig: pub fn fill_triangle(self: Canvas, tx0: integer, ty0: integer, tx1: integer, ty1: integer, tx2: integer, ty2: integer, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a triangle with vertices (tx0,ty0), (tx1,ty1), (tx2,ty2).
Uses flat-top/flat-bottom decomposition with scanline fill.

api.sig: pub struct Coord
api.doc:
A point on the canvas, in pixels.

Exists because a polygon is a LIST of them and `fill_triangle`'s six loose
integers do not generalise — six is already the edge of what a caller gets
right in order, and a polygon has no fixed count.

NOT called `Point`: `mesh3d::LightType` has a `Point` variant and `graphics`
depends on mesh3d, so the name is taken and the collision is a hard error
("struct 'Point' conflicts with a enumvalue of the same name"). `Vertex` is
mesh3d's too. Reach for `Coord` in 2-D graphics code and the 3-D names stay
where they belong.

api.sig: pub fn fill_polygon(self: Canvas, pts: const vector<Coord>, color: integer)
api.doc:
Fill a closed polygon under the EVEN-ODD rule.

The polygon closes itself: the last point joins the first, so a triangle is
three points and not four. Fewer than three points draws nothing.

Even-odd means a point is inside when a ray from it crosses the outline an odd
number of times, so a self-intersecting outline leaves its overlap EMPTY — the
classic five-point star is a pentagon-shaped hole with five filled arms. That
is a choice, not a bug: the alternative (non-zero winding) fills the middle,
and the two disagree on exactly the shapes people draw deliberately.

Matches `fill_triangle` pixel for pixel on a triangle, which is the reason the
row rule below is inclusive rather than the half-open rule a scanline filler
usually takes. See the note on `polygon_crossings`.
Example: @GFX-006 — the star's hollow middle, and the triangle agreement.

api.sig: pub fn resize_lanczos(self: const Canvas, ow: integer, oh: integer) -> Canvas
api.doc:
Resample this canvas to `ow` x `oh` with a Lanczos-3 filter.

Byte-identical to Pillow's `Image.resize(..., Image.LANCZOS)`, which is the
point: the `.draw` corpus renders at 3x and downscales with exactly that, so a
renderer that resamples any other way cannot be pixel-compared against it
however good it looks (@PLN146 W0 finding 5).

**Alpha is premultiplied across the resample and undone after**, because
Pillow defines `resize` on an image with alpha as
`convert("RGBa") -> resize -> convert("RGBA")`. That is a contract, not an
optimisation: resampling straight RGBA lets a transparent texel's colour bleed
into its neighbours, and the two disagree on any edge where alpha varies.
Both roundings are Pillow's and neither is the obvious one — `(v*a + 127)/255`
going in, a TRUNCATING divide coming out, and alpha 0 passes its colour
through untouched rather than going black.
Example: @GFX-007 — why a 3x supersample plus this is not the same picture as
drawing once at final size.

api.sig: pub fn resize_bicubic(self: const Canvas, ow: integer, oh: integer) -> Canvas
api.doc:
Resample with a BICUBIC filter — Pillow's `Image.resize` default.

The default is the reason this exists: `resize(size)` with no `resample=`
argument is bicubic, and code that builds a small image and enlarges it (a
gradient computed at 100x100, say) takes that path without naming it. Read
the call site's filter off the ARGUMENT LIST and it looks like there isn't
one.

⚠ Bicubic has negative lobes, so an ENLARGEMENT overshoots: a hard 40→200
step upscaled 4x spans 28..212 in Pillow and here alike. That is the filter,
not a defect — clamping it away would be the defect.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Canvas, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Save canvas as a PNG file. Automatically uses RGBA if any pixel has alpha < 255,

Example: @GFX-005 — the choice is read off the pixels, so ONE alpha-0 pixel
(a hand-written hex literal — @GFX-001) makes the whole file RGBA and that

api.doc:

api.doc:

api.sig: pub struct Pixel
api.doc:
Data per pixel of a PNG image.
Fields r, g, b hold red, green and blue intensity, each 0–255.  The channels
are const, so a pixel is REPLACED (`img.data[i] = Pixel{…}`), never edited in
place, and `limit(0, 255)` is a range rather than a clamp — a value outside it
stores 0.
Example: @IMG-003 — replacing a pixel, and why the local you read it into is a
view of its slot rather than a snapshot.
Example: @IMG-004 — the range is not a clamp: doubling a bright channel stores
0, so brightening turns the brightest pixels black.

api.sig: pub fn value(self: Pixel) -> integer
api.doc:
Returns the pixel colour as a packed 24-bit integer (0xRRGGBB).
Use for fast colour comparison or storage.

api.sig: pub struct Image
api.doc:
Database structure with image data.
The actual data is in height rows of width length: `data` is one FLAT vector in
row-major order, so the pixel at (x, y) is `data[y * width + x]`, and
`len(data) == width * height` always holds on an image `png()` handed back.
Example: @IMG-001 — the addressing rule, and what the null check buys.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Image, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc: Write this image to a PNG file. Returns true on success.

api.sig: pub fn png(self: File) -> Image
api.doc:
Decodes a PNG file and returns an Image.
Returns null when there is nothing to decode — the path does not exist, names
a directory, or holds bytes this decoder cannot read.  So the answer is either
a complete image (`len(data) == width * height`) or null; there is no
half-filled Image to guard against.  Any PNG colour type loads: RGBA, greyscale
and palette files are folded to RGB, alpha discarded.
Use to load sprite sheets or textures.
Example: @IMG-001 — the three ways to get null, and the completeness the null
check buys past it.
Example: @IMG-002 — every colour type arrives as RGB; alpha is DISCARDED, so a
sprite sheet needs a colour key rather than a transparency test.

api.sig: pub struct Pixel
api.doc:
Data per pixel of a PNG image.
Fields r, g, b hold red, green and blue intensity and `a` holds opacity, each
0–255.  The channels are const, so a pixel is REPLACED (`img.data[i] =
Pixel{…}`), never edited in place, and `limit(0, 255)` is a range rather than a
clamp — a value outside it stores 0.

**`a` defaults to 255, and the default is load-bearing.** An omitted field takes
its type's zero, and zero alpha is INVISIBLE — so without the declared default
every `Pixel{r, g, b}` ever written would silently become fully transparent
(loft#914's `omitted-field-zero` in its purest form).  With it, code that
predates alpha keeps meaning what it meant: opaque.
Example: @IMG-003 — replacing a pixel, and why the local you read it into is a
view of its slot rather than a snapshot.
Example: @IMG-004 — the range is not a clamp: doubling a bright channel stores
0, so brightening turns the brightest pixels black.

api.sig: pub fn value(self: Pixel) -> integer
api.doc:
Returns the pixel colour as a packed 24-bit integer (0xRRGGBB).
Use for fast colour comparison or storage.  Alpha is NOT in it — this is the
pre-alpha contract and stays 24-bit, so a comparison written against it keeps
answering what it answered.  For opacity read `p.a`, or `rgba()` for the packed
32-bit form.

api.sig: pub fn rgba(self: Pixel) -> integer
api.doc:
Returns the pixel as a packed 32-bit integer (0xAARRGGBB) — the byte order
`graphics::Canvas` uses, so a decoded image can be handed to a canvas without a
per-channel loop at the call site.

api.sig: pub fn opaque(self: Pixel, cutoff: integer = 128) -> boolean
api.doc:
Is this texel opaque enough to count as covered?

A collision proxy, a trim box and a colour key all want the same question, and
they want it with a THRESHOLD rather than `a == 255`: antialiased art has a
fringe of partly-transparent texels that belong to the silhouette.  Default 128
— half opacity — which is the midpoint of that fringe.

api.sig: pub struct Image
api.doc:
Database structure with image data.
The actual data is in height rows of width length: `data` is one FLAT vector in
row-major order, so the pixel at (x, y) is `data[y * width + x]`, and
`len(data) == width * height` always holds on an image `png()` handed back.
Example: @IMG-001 — the addressing rule, and what the null check buys.

api.sig: pub fn save_png(self: const Image, path: text) -> boolean
api.doc: Write this image to a PNG file. Returns true on success.

api.sig: pub fn png(self: File) -> Image
api.doc:
Decodes a PNG file and returns an Image.
Returns null when there is nothing to decode — the path does not exist, names
a directory, or holds bytes this decoder cannot read.  So the answer is either
a complete image (`len(data) == width * height`) or null; there is no
half-filled Image to guard against.  Any PNG colour type loads: greyscale and
palette files are expanded to RGBA, and **alpha is carried** — a file with no
alpha channel arrives fully opaque (`a == 255`), never transparent.
Use to load sprite sheets or textures.
Example: @IMG-001 — the three ways to get null, and the completeness the null
check buys past it.
Example: @IMG-002 — every colour type arrives as RGBA, and a source without an
alpha channel is opaque rather than invisible.

api.sig: pub struct WsHandler
pub fn ws_handler(url: text) -> WsHandler
api.doc:
Open a WebSocket session.  Returns null only if the URL is
malformed; transient connection failures (server not yet up,
network blip) are absorbed by the auto-reconnect loop in the Rust
layer, so this call always returns a usable handle for any
well-formed `ws://...` URL.

api.sig: pub fn send(self: WsHandler, msg: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Send a text message to the server.  Returns true on success; false
means the connection is currently in backoff / reconnecting and the
caller may retry after the next `pump()`.

api.sig: pub fn send_binary(self: WsHandler, msg: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Send `msg` as a binary WebSocket frame (opcode 2).  Loft `text`
is a byte buffer — pack u8/u16/i32/etc. into it via `to_bytes`
style code, then ship it.  Returns true on success; false means
the connection is currently in backoff / reconnecting.

api.sig: pub fn last_opcode(self: WsHandler) -> integer
api.doc:
Opcode of the last frame surfaced by `try_recv` / `pump` on this
handler.  Use after a successful read to decide whether to
interpret the payload as utf-8 text or as a binary blob.

api.sig: pub fn pump(self: WsHandler, on_message: fn(text)) -> integer
api.doc:
Drain any pending received messages, firing `on_message` for each.
Returns the count of messages delivered this call.  Call this from
a main loop (and yield to the host between iterations on the browser
target) to drive event delivery without async.

api.sig: pub fn try_recv(self: WsHandler) -> text?
api.doc:
Non-blocking single-message receive.  Returns the next pending
message text if one is available, null otherwise.  Equivalent to a
single iteration of pump without the callback — useful when the
receiver wants to drive its own loop and accumulate messages
locally without capturing state inside a closure.

api.sig: pub fn close(self: WsHandler)
api.doc: Permanently close the session (no further reconnect attempts).

api.sig: pub fn sleep_ms(ms: integer)
api.doc:
Block the calling thread for `ms` milliseconds.  Convenience for
tests and pacing loops; non-positive values are a no-op.  Not
available on the WASM target — the host event loop is the
equivalent.

api.sig: pub fn pack_reset()
api.doc: Empty the per-thread pack buffer.  Call before each blob.

api.sig: pub fn pack_u8(b: integer)
api.doc: Append a single byte to the pack buffer.  `b` is masked to 8 bits.

api.sig: pub fn pack_u16_le(v: integer)
api.doc: Append a 2-byte little-endian unsigned value.

api.sig: pub fn pack_u32_le(v: integer)
api.doc:
Append a 4-byte little-endian unsigned value.  Loft `integer` is
i32 — bit-cast to u32 to preserve the LE byte pattern across the
sign boundary.

api.sig: pub fn pack_take() -> text
api.doc:
Take the contents of the pack buffer and return them as a `text`
whose UTF-8 bytes are exactly the buffer bytes.  Resets the buffer.

api.sig: pub fn byte_at(idx: integer, t: text) -> integer
api.doc:
Read the byte at `idx` of the text payload.  Out-of-range (negative
or past the end) returns -1.  Use to decode binary frames received
via `try_recv` / `pump`.  Argument order is (idx, t) — the C-ABI
auto-marshal in src/extensions.rs supports (I32, Text) -> I32 but
not (Text, I32) -> I32.
